strings.en: A Dirad officer serving Diore. Fiercely proud of being Dirad, he looks down on humans, so he's always wary of Shapiro, once a human, and dislikes him.
A Dirad officer like Abel, but far gentler in temperament. Drawn to Shapiro, a human, the kind the Dirad hold in contempt.
An instructor at Shinobu's military academy, and once Sara's lover. Cool-headed, and a gifted strategist and tactician. He urged the brass to prepare for an alien attack,
but was ignored, and when aliens came, the army's failure disgusted him. He forsook Earth for the alien Muge Zorbados Empire. As a Muge staff officer, he leaked Earth's intel
and preyed on human weakness against the Cyber Beast Force, but defeats cost him his Muge standing. Fighting to regain it, he fell to his ex, Sara, amid ambition and madness.
A bio-high-tech authority who built the Cyber Beast machines. At first baffled by Shinobu and co.'s wild ways, he came to understand them well. He seems cold, but he took in
war orphan Laura, and has nerve too, firing a machine gun when the base was attacked. Once the deputy, he became commander after Commander Igor died
and led the Cyber Beast Force.
Leader of the Cyber Beast Force. A natural at aerial combat, he seems born to fly his beloved Eagle Fighter. Quick to pick fights, he goes right at anyone
he doesn't like. But he has no hidden side, so once he opens up, he's a great friend. Though a soldier, he talks casually to his superiors, and disobeying orders is his specialty.
In Dancougar he says heartbreak, setbacks and his father drove him to enlist. Always fighting with teammate Sara, yet they care for each other. Catchphrase: "Let's do this!"
A Cyber Beast Force member, pilot of the Land Cougar. Shinobu's academy classmate, she loved their instructor Shapiro. But he defected to the Muge Zorbados Empire,
and when she tried to follow, Shinobu stopped her. Torn between love and hate, she fights Shapiro, finally defeating him herself and leaving her past behind. Fiery like her teammates,
she often hits before she talks. She and Shinobu care for each other, confirming it as the story goes on.
A member of the Cyber Beast Force and pilot of the Big Moth. The calmest man on the team, with superb judgment. But he's a bit of a cynic, and he and the hotheaded Shinobu
were always clashing. Still, his advice was usually spot-on, making him the team's linchpin. A master of Chinese kenpo, he put it to use piloting his Cyber Beast machine.
He later proposed to and married Daniela, a girl he met during the war.
The youngest of the Cyber Beast Force, he pilots the Land Liger. A cheerful joker and the team's mood-maker, but in battle he's as fierce as the rest.
Defying his father, head of a military firm, he enlisted. A ladies' man, he fell at first sight for Laura, the war orphan Shinobu took in. He claims he's better in combat than in practice.
Also, his baseball skill reportedly amazes even married women.
The Muge Empire's emperor. From the Muge universe, another universe (dimension), he invades the solar system. In the original, his evil spirits from Muge Castle plague Dancougar,
but falls to the Danku Sword, thrown in a do-or-die gamble. However...
Queen of the Dirad, plant people of a plant planet. Nearing Earth to retry "something" that failed 200 million years ago, she revived the drifting Shapiro as a useful pawn.
Quiet and lenient with subordinates, but not human, so her true depths can't be known.
Head of the space crime syndicate Gyandlar. A villain who roams space doing evil and trusts only himself. Seeking the Hyper Libido, a super energy said to grant eternal life,
he attacked Cronos, but Rom and the Cronos warriors foiled him.
A Gyandlar officer, practically Gades's right hand. Not just skilled in combat but also cunning, with a warrior's pride to match. Rom's fated rival.
His sword Nagase resembles Kenrou.
Gyandlar officer Gardy's true form: Rom and Leina's real older brother, thought to have died young. Taken in by Gades for his Tenku Shinken talent, he long served as an officer
under mind control. (The fearsome Gardy look was likely part of it.) In the original's finale, he gives his sword to his beloved brother Rom and tells him to slay Gades.
Daughter of Demon Commander Jingi, beaten by Rom in episode 7. Honorable and kind like her father, but Diondra tricks her into thinking Rom killed Jingi foully, so with brother Colon
she hunts Rom to avenge him. Together they combine with the giant buffalo mecha Jingi Mark II.
Kina's brother, Jingi's son. Hunts Rom with his sister. Very nimble.
A Gyandlar officer who loves dirty tricks and schemes, the Gyandlar's strategist. In the original, Rom beats him in the battle at Tenku Majo, but he returns as a spirit
and plagues Rom's group to the end.
A master swordsman hired by the Gyandlar. Having lost his purpose in a world without war, he sells his sword to them. His skill in the deadly Dark Twin Slayer Sword
rivals Jet's Tenku Shinken. A true warrior who disdains dirty fighting.
A female Gyandlar officer. Unlike Grujios, she usually commands directly at the front. Devil Saturn is her direct subordinate. She wields a whip, and her talk and manner
fit, but don't call her 'Big Sis'!
The Gyandlar Demon Commander who leads "Devil Saturn 6." (Devil Saturn 6 is formed when six units, No. 1 to 6, combine.) Always sent in ahead of the Gyandlar strike forces,
and is usually beaten by Rom's group. With his odd Kansai dialect and gracious exits, he's hard to hate.
Leina's Machine Robo aide: robot, copter or supercar. A poor fighter, he humbly backs up tomboy Leina (and gets dragged along).
Former top disciple of Kirai Stol, Rom's master and father, making him Rom's senior, a Cronos native. He learned Tenku Chushin Ken, but Kirai saw he craved power over heart
and denied him full mastery. Bitter, he fled to become a bandit. He uses the Electromagnetic Poison Hand Blade, a forbidden Tenku Chushin Ken move.
A Jet clan warrior who trained under Kirai with Rom and Drill, and learned Tenku Shinken from him. As the name says, he becomes a jet. The cool, handsome one of Rom's group,
he swoops in crying "Jeeet!" when friends or beauties are in danger.
Rom's sister. Cheerful, active, and a bit too devoted to her brother, with Jim as her attendant. She knows some Tenku Chushin Ken, if less than Rom. Treated like a princess until midway,
she later boards the Power Riser and actively joins the fight.
Fellow disciple of Rom and Jet. Of the Battle clan, he turns into a drill tank. Cheerful and bold, he loves power moves. The group's mood-maker, his drill saved his friends many times.
A Cronos clan warrior and martial artist. With the Tenku Chushin Ken and Tenku Shinken of his father Kirai, he cuts down evil. Just, polite, hard on himself, a bit soft on sister Leina.
With his father's sword Kenrou, he becomes the robot Kenryu or Baikanfu. His Tenku Chushin Ken and speeches from nowhere scare villains stiff. With Jet, Drill and Leina,
he beats the Gyandlar, who seek the Hyper Libido, and is reborn anew.
Leader of the space pirate Bunker. With four top lieutenants and countless minions, he rules space lawlessly. Asking Dr. Tarsan for the ultimate robot started the original.
Linked to a Dangaioh member, but...
Once under Tarsan, joined the Bunker to replace the Dangaioh team after they fled Tarsan. Cold and ruthless. Toward the Dangaioh team, favored over this pilot,
especially Mia Alice, harbors hostility, rivalry, and even murderous intent.
Handmaid to the royal family of planet Lilith, she became a hired warrior after the Bunker attacked. The royals surrendered, the people suffered... and Lilith was destroyed.
Shazara is one of its victims too. Told that a royal, Lamba Nom, is on the Dangaioh team, she attacks Dangaioh for revenge.
A Bunker warrior paired with Flash. Once in the resistance against the Bunker on planet Latesia, but defected when the tide turned, and with Flash betrayed
and killed their leader, Roll.
A Bunker warrior paired with Burst. Saps Roll's will by reviving the nightmare of being betrayed and killed by trusted comrades. Flash and Burst look beautiful,
but are utterly vile; in the original, the Psychic Wave crushes them.
Dangaioh's main pilot, a psychic who generates energy by running. Usually a timid boy, but once Dangaioh combines he does a 180 and turns bold and reliable.
He seems the most ordinary of the four, but his sealed memories hide a terrible past...?
An Earth-born girl on the Dangaioh team. Her power is uncontrollable but the team's strongest (blasting foes, teleporting, flying, as needed). Kind and peace-loving, but
chosen for the Dangaioh team, she fled Tarsan and was dragged into war with the space pirates, the Bunker. Tarsan wiped the team's memories, but
Mia recalls Earth is her home, so the four set their aimless escape for Earth. There's talk of a lost brother and a strange power in her...?
On the Dangaioh team; a psychic who shoots lasers from her fingers (and ran dry fast in the original). Rides the Dan Mechanic forming Dangaioh's arms; her cockpit is the right arm.
(She screams at Boost Knuckle because her cockpit flies off with the fist.) The youngest of the four. Cheerful mood-maker of the team, but apparently of noble birth...
On the Dangaioh team; her psychic power(?) is absurd strength. Rides the Dan Mechanic forming the legs. Rough-talking and pushy, the big sister who leads the team.
Like the others, her origins are shrouded in mystery.
Dangaioh's creator, a space-roving scientist. Hired by the Bunker's boss, Grand Captain Garimos, he built Dangaioh and gathered its team from space. Calculating; hardly a good man.
But kind at heart, which shows in his words and deeds; with his scatterbrained side, he's hard to hate. He altered the team's memories so they believe he created them.
When the team turned on the Bunker, Tarsan, their maker, was hunted too, so he travels with them.
The Nadesico's likable vice-captain. In the original, an officer cadet on the Alliance's elite track, but he boarded the private warship Nadesico for Yurika, whom he loves.
Sadly, Yurika sees him only as a "good friend." He's had IFS nanomachine treatment and can pilot an Aestivalis.
In the original, the pilot who replaced the fallen Yamada. Long-haired, smug, yet truly skilled: a textbook heartthrob. Like Erina, who came aboard with him, he seems fishy.
Captain of the Kannazuki, Superior Human Corps. Pilots the Denjin. Friend of Shiratori and Tsukiomi. Looks goofy but is a sharp strategist. In the original, tried to sink the Nadesico.
Often covers for the reckless Saburota, but seems quite fond of him.
One of the Nadesico's three female Aestivalis pilots; the one with glasses. Cheery anime fan who makes doujinshi. In the original, Uribatake taught her modeling.
Supreme commander of the Superior Human Corps. Leads the war on "evil" Earth for the justice he believes in.
Captain of the Yumemizuki, Superior Human Corps. Pilots the Tetsujin. A typical Jovian who treats Gekiganger 3 as scripture: hot-blooded and pure. In the original, foes of peace plot
his tragic death.
One of the Nadesico's three female Aestivalis pilots; the one with short hair. The trio's leader, rough-talking but pure-hearted. Has feelings for Akito.
A Nadesico Aestivalis pilot, real name "Jiro Yamada." A hardcore Gekiganger 3 fan who takes "Gai Daigoji" as his soul name. Hot blood walking on two legs,
but often spins his wheels; in the original he ended up as comic relief.
Vice-captain of the Kannazuki and Genpachiro's aide. Reckless, he charges in, crashes, and often needs Genpachiro to bail him out.
A Superior Human Corps commander and Tsukumo's friend. Pilots the Mazin. Looks gentle, but will cast off anything for his idea of justice. A master of Jovian jujutsu.
A young man who wants to be a real cook. Mars-born, he joins the Nadesico as an apprentice cook after meeting his old friend Yurika. Having IFS, he ends up an Aestivalis pilot.
A Gekiganger 3 fan who gets along with Yamada. When the Jovian Lizards struck Mars's Utopia Colony, he was caught in a blast and somehow appeared on Earth.
Perhaps thanks to his honesty, he's a hit; many Nadesico women love him.
The Nadesico's helmsman, with the best figure on the crew. A secretary before joining the Nadesico. A grown woman in every way, personality included,
but fragile when she breaks.
The Nadesico's ever-calm operator, whose catchphrase is "Bunch of idiots." Specially educated from childhood, she and the ship's learning computer Omoikane
share a true meeting of hearts. She seems antisocial, but just doesn't know how to relate to people; she ponders life far more deeply than others her age.
One of the Nadesico's three female Aestivalis pilots. Intentionally or not, she loves lame jokes, and can pull a ukulele out of nowhere to go with them.
At times she flips to an ultra-serious mode, unlike her usual flightiness. It may relate to losing two fiances to death.
The Nadesico's young captain. Mars-born and proud of her figure. Unshakably goes at her own pace; means no harm, but drags everyone along. A skilled tactician, though.
Daughter of Earth Alliance (original) Admiral Koichiro Misumaru. She openly adores her old friend Akito, which frustrates the other women on the crew who like him.
The Nadesico's comms officer, formerly a voice actress and nurse. Likes Akito and sees Yurika as a rival. Usually quiet, but when it comes to Akito
she gets assertive.
A girl Akito failed to save on Mars's Utopia Colony, which he long regretted. She's actually young Inez; or rather, Inez is Ai all grown up.
A biological Boson Jump sent her into the past, where Nergal, then in early development, took her in.
A Nergal researcher and "explaining lady" who loves making others understand, though she's only 28. Also produces "Why? How? Nadesico," a special broadcast on big events.
Analyzes things calmly, but seems to hide some secret in her past.
The Nadesico's chief mechanic; ran a small factory before being scouted. Loves tinkering and is a skilled modeler. Builds many mechs and gadgets aboard on Nergal's budget.
Dream line: "I prepared for just this!" In the original he fell for Hikaru and was rejected. He has a wife and kids.
A relief sub-helmsman sent to the Nadesico. An ambitious elite aiming to top Nergal within 3 years, clearly out of place at the "front" or a "worksite." Who is she really...?
In the original, after many misfires among the Nadesico's oddballs, she grows fond of Akito.
Tsukumo Shiratori's sister, a Jovian girl with a brother complex. Unusual among the Jovians, she hates anime.
The Nadesico's auditor. "Prospector" is a code name; his real name is unknown. Space abacus in hand, he frets over the cost of the Nadesico's wild antics.
Minds costs and the Nadesico's place in Nergal, but is good at heart. Has a special skill(?): running a ramen stall.
Yurika's father; originally admiral of the Alliance 3rd Fleet. Loves his daughter boundlessly, or rather dotes hopelessly. A solid admiral, though.
Boards the Nadesico as admiral to push Nergal's wishes. Snide and resented by most of the crew. In the original he even shot Jiro Yamada,
among other incidents.
The growth-type computer at the Nadesico's core. Advanced enough to have a self, it's Ruri's confidant. Super-A-class performance. Named after a god of wisdom
in Japanese myth. Its emblem is a bronze bell bearing its name in kanji.
The Elshank's ex-commander. He adored Romina, but as she took to Joe and his failures mounted, Hazard's men preyed on him; bent on revenge on Joe, he joined the Za Boom Army.
Proud; even as an enemy, he scorns dirty tactics.
Annex's female aide. Uses swordplay and illusions and leads a kunoichi squad. Cold, but loves beauty, and schemes to take Earth for herself.
A Mars settler boy who moved there from Japan with his father as a child. A classic hothead: foul-mouthed, short-tempered. (In the original, that drove Ilbora from the Elshank.)
In the original, on his 16th birthday (Mars's coming of age), he butted into the Elshank's arrival on Mars and was chosen as Kurojishi's pilot.
Once a polar-cap outlaw on Mars, he joins Joe seeking the outside world. Even Joe, a top brawler at the base, can't beat him. Like Joe, rough-mouthed but kind at heart.
He always regrets that he can't pilot a machine to help, but in the original he proved himself in close combat and spy work.
A mysterious ninja robot with a will of its own, appearing from nowhere when the Elshank or Kurojishi's trio are in peril. Shema legend says "the Za Boom star
was destroyed by a ninja"; Romina and Annex both seek its power...
Commander of the Mars Frontier Base. In the original, a demotion to the frontier, so he resents Earth's government and vows to show them. Then, chasing the Elshank to Mars,
the Za Boom Army came, and he secretly sought their power for his ambition. (As base commander, he has the base's troops.) Servile to the strong, bullying to the weak,
a classic mastermind villain, skilled at backroom deals. Uses dirty tactics without a qualm, yet has a goofy side.
Joe's sidekick, pilot of the Blast Dragon, always tagging after Joe. Very timid, but maybe thanks to Joe he blurts things out or acts tough, often causing trouble.
He likes Romina's aide, Shaff.
Joe's childhood friend, a year older: a feisty tomboy. Like Joe and Mike, she's chosen by Houraiou to fight. She's sweet on Joe,
and always frets as he and Romina grow closer.
Princess of planet Radorio in the Shema system. To stop Annex, she came in the Elshank to solve the "ninja legend" of great power; her crash-landing on Mars
began Joe's battles. Gentle and graceful, yet so naturally candid she acts without hesitation. She trusts Joe, a reliable alien warrior, and comes to love him.
The Elshank's commander after Ilbora left (his aide before). Crude and short-tempered as he looks, always clashing with Joe. He worships Ilbora; even after he joined the Za Boom,
he wished to serve him.
Romina's lady-in-waiting. Calm and unsung, she warmly supports the naive Romina. In the original she even acted boldly as Romina's body double.
Emperor of the Za Boom Army. Blaming the Shema system's decline on waning fighting instinct, he seeks to conquer space. Fearing the legend that a ninja destroyed Za Boom, he
also seeks the ninja's power.
Joe's old best friend, a Major in Earth's government. Upright and earnest, but as Joe's friend he can act boldly. In the original, his father ran the Mars base before Hazard.
He helps Joe expose Hazard's plot.
A Zeon test pilot; sister of Ginias, head of the Apsaras Project. The Sahalins were once a great Zeon house. Testing mobile suits in space, she clashed with the Federation,
and fatefully met Shiro Amada, then en route to Earth. Having volunteered for her brother, she's no great soldier, but a woman of hidden inner strength.
She fears her brother's abnormal obsession with the Apsaras Project.
Aina's brother, head of the Apsaras Project. Wasting from a grave illness, he's morbidly obsessed with finishing his giant mobile armor Apsaras and restoring the fallen Sahalins.
A young officer sent to lead the 08th MS Team. Inexperienced, he won his men's trust by action and completed his missions without losing a man. Meeting Aina Sahalin,
he wrestles with war's realities, but fights on for what he believes.
A longtime Sahalin retainer. A top MS pilot and a cool, stern warrior. Like a parent to Aina; to grant her wish of sending the wounded home to space,
he charges the foe alone and dies.
Daughter of a guerrilla chief who rose in the chaos of war. In the original, Shiro seeks her help against a Zeon unit. Frank, and despite her looks, a skilled fighter.
A Side 6-born Federation pilot, rank Lieutenant. On the team building the Newtype Gundam NT-1 Alex. Raised well-off, she's gentle: the "girl next door" type.
Her job: giving untested machines a veteran's combat skill (a "shoe fitter"). But short-staffed, she was also the Alex's test pilot.
In the Chobham-armored NT-1 Alex she routed the Cyclops Team sent to steal it. A week later she fought Bernie's Zaku II Kai and, though the Alex was wrecked, won.
Chris never learned who piloted that Zaku II Kai.
Drafted out of high school, he became a Zeon mobile suit pilot, rank Corporal. After his first battle he joined Steiner's Cyclops Team as a replacement.
In the raid to steal the NT-1 Alex on Side 6, his mistake doomed it; all the Cyclops Team but him died. He bonded with Christina Mackenzie and a colony boy, Alfred Izuruha
(Al). So to stop the brass from destroying the colony if the Alex couldn't be stolen, he set out, with Al's urging and help, to beat the NT-1 Alex.
He wrecked the Alex, but its Beam Saber pierced his cockpit, and he died...
A Zeon ace since the One Year War, rank Major. His Gelgoog's huge haul at Solomon earned him the name "the Nightmare of Solomon."
His name is even in Federation academy textbooks. Devoted to Zeon's ideals, he joined the Delaz Fleet after the war. A key figure in Operation Stardust,
he did much to carry it out. But in the chaos of Cima's betrayal, while joining the Axis fleet, he rammed a Federation warship and died in space.
An ex-Zeon Captain who lost an arm in the One Year War; Gato's comrade. Ran a junk shop in Von Braun on the moon, but secretly fixed the mobile armor Val Walo to join the Delaz Fleet.
He met Kou, who'd left the army in despair. Repaying Kelly's hospitality, Kou helped though he knew Kelly was Zeon, and the Val Walo was finished. But his contact Cima wanted only
the Val Walo, and the deal fell through. To live as a warrior, he fought Kou's Gundam GP01Fb on the moon, but lost to Kou's bold tactics.
A test pilot training at the Federation's Torrington base in Australia, rank Lieutenant. He saw Gato steal the Gundam GP02A and volunteered to get it back.
Versed in mobile suits, he amazed Nina by spotting at a glance that the GP02A carried a nuke. In his first battle Gato saw through his inexperience and humiliated him,
but his talent bloomed until he could face Gato as an equal. Shy even at Nijmegen academy, known for rich boys, he let Nina lead in their romance.
Hates carrots.
A Federation veteran who led Monsha and others since the One Year War, rank Captain. Caught up in the GP02A theft, he became mobile suit commander
of the pursuit ship Albion. In space training he met Cima's unit; he drove it off, but his damaged mech exploded on the way back. Stern but warm, loved by every Albion
pilot. He had a wife on Earth, living apart.
A Zeon Lieutenant Colonel. Since the One Year War she did the dirty work, like gassing colonies. A formidable captain of the Zanzibar-class Lili Marleen, but her naked
ambition made Gato distrust her. Indeed, in the Delaz Fleet she secretly dealt with the Federation and Anaheim, selling the colony drop plan for her own safety.
At last she seized Delaz's ship Gwaden. Meaning to hand him over, she shot him and fled the Gwaden in a Gerbera Tetra. But she met Kou's Gundam GP03 Dendrobium,
and fell to its Mega Beam Cannon.
An Anaheim Electronics engineer and Lunarian (moon dweller), lent to the Federation for the Gundam project. She saw the GP02A stolen at Torrington, and until the
conflict ended, stayed with the Albion. Drawn to Kou's talent, she's tormented to learn his foe is her old lover, Gato.
Once a Titan, she joined the AEUG by her own convictions, rank Lieutenant. Intellectual, but competitive and strong-willed, she always tries to act like a big sister
to the younger Kamille, Katz and Fa. Henken loved her, and she didn't seem to mind. Gravely hurt fighting Reccoa, who'd gone to Scirocco, she died with Kamille at her side.
A civilian boy in Green Noa 1, a Side 7 colony. Hobbies: karate, flying the Homo Abyss (a one-man glider), junior mobile suits, etc. Touchy about his girlish name,
he punched Jerid for mocking it and was hauled off by the Titans. Meeting Quattro, who had slipped into Green Noa, he joined the AEUG. On his first ride in the Gundam Mk-II,
he fought so well Bright and others called him "Amuro Ray reborn." In the AEUG he won many battles and, as his Newtype powers bloomed, fought like an ace.
He also had design talent: the Mk-II's Flying Armor and the Zeta Gundam use his ideas. His nature is complex: sensitive yet violent, boyishly candid yet calculating.
At first he fought from vague anger at the Titans, but meeting Quattro, Amuro and Four, he came to fight by his own will to end the war, and grew greatly as a person.
He beat Scirocco in the final battle at the colony laser, but his mind broke. He then recovered with Fa, and in Gundam ZZ guided Judau and Ple several times.
He recovers in that show's finale.
The Argama's mobile suit leader. Only a Captain, but he flies the Rick Dias and Hyaku Shiki and shapes strategy: a key AEUG figure. Always in sunglasses; his words and past
are a mystery. He is in fact Zeon's Red Comet, Char Aznable, sent from Axis to scout the Earth Sphere. Noting Kamille's Newtype potential early,
he looks after him in many ways. At first he just piloted against the Titans, foes of spacenoids, but after old rival Amuro, Scirocco's rise, Blex's death and the Dakar speech,
he became the AEUG's leading figure. But after fighting Haman's Qubeley at the colony laser, he vanished. Char never used the name Quattro again. "Quattro" is Italian for "4,"
meaning his fourth name, after Casval, Edward and Char.
A Titans officer, rank Lieutenant. Proud of his elite status, he looks down on others. Mocking Kamille's name starts trouble, and via Bask's scheme he kills Kamille's mother Hilda.
After his comrades and lover are shot down one by one, he hunts Kamille as his nemesis. At last he challenges Kamille in the Bound Doc, but dies in the blast of Henken's Radish.
Regent to Mineva Zabi, ruler of Axis. Her father, Maharaja Khan, led Zeon's fleet that fled the Earth Sphere. After his death, her strong charisma held Axis together.
Seeking to rule the Earth Sphere, she moved Axis there and contacted both the AEUG and the Titans. Breaking with the AEUG over Quattro, she aimed to profit after their final battle.
In Gundam ZZ, exploiting the Federation's weakness, she founded Neo Zeon as its real leader. She took the Federation Congress in Dakar bloodlessly, but with Glemy's revolt,
her ambition was never fulfilled. In the end she lost a duel with Judau's ZZ Gundam and died. She believed Newtypes would change society, but her means were
rejected by Quattro, Kamille and Judau. Yet her twisted ways came from duty and loneliness; at heart she longed for Char, her old anchor, to return. A superb Newtype and pilot,
she flies the Qubeley, Neo Zeon's very symbol. And like Char, she rarely wore a normal suit in battle.
The girl next door to Kamille on Green Noa 1. After the Titans seized her parents, she joined the AEUG as a pilot. On Green Noa 1, she fussed over Kamille out of affection,
but in the AEUG, fear made her lean on him. Wanting his approval, she often pushed too hard as a pilot. To nurse Kamille, his mind broken in the final battle with Scirocco,
she leaves the Argama early in Gundam ZZ.
A Titans member and first-rate pilot who handles high-mobility units like the Gaplant and Hambrabi at will. Also a schemer: aboard the Alexandria,
he had Jamaican murdered. Drawn to Scirocco's grand vision, he aids him. Teamed with Ramsus and Dangel, he torments Quattro and Kamille, but Kamille, enraged by his cruelty,
triggered the Zeta Gundam's bio-sensor and shot him down. Yet in Gundam ZZ episode 1 he reaches Shangri-La in Side 1 and tries to steal mobile suits from the docked Argama,
where his cruelty enrages Judau too. Then, with junk dealer Gemon Bajack, he hits the Argama in the Geze, but Judau's Zeta Gundam downs him.
A Cyber-Newtype tuned at the Augusta Newtype lab. Her One Year War colony drop trauma was used to make the AEUG her enemy. She attacks the Audhumla in a Gaplant,
but Katz and Kamille shoot her down. Retuned to see Kamille as her brother, she meets him in Side 2 under Gates's control. Finally, she attacks the Argama in the Psyco Gundam Mk-II,
but by then repeated tuning had nearly broken her mind.
A Neo Zeon officer, aide to Mashymre after he became a Cyber-Newtype, tasked with watching him. A Newtype herself, she flies the mobile suit Re-Gelgu,
and briefly bonded with Judau.
One of the Shangri-La junk-dealer gang, mainly in charge of intel. Lively and feisty, she squabbles with Judau but secretly likes him.
On the Argama, she burns with rivalry toward Roux and mostly flies the Gundam Mk-II. In battle she shows Judau her girlish side at times, but in the end she
returns Beecha's feelings.
A girl conditioned at Axis as a Newtype pilot. She takes to Judau at once and joins the Argama once Glemy's mind control is broken.
Loves chocolate parfaits and baths. Day to day she's a little girl whose childish whims and jealousy trouble Judau and co. But inside, raised as a warrior, she's full of loneliness.
Blaming herself for Leina going missing, she tries to be Judau's support, but dies fighting Ple Two.
A Neo Zeon officer. After fighting under Mashymre, he was given a unit by Haman. Later, claiming Zabi blood, he plots as figurehead to topple Haman and restore the Zabis.
At first, in the original, a rich boy smitten with Roux, but as his ambition grew, readying a Newtype unit and winning over Rakan and others, he showed his cold, ruthless cunning.
At the end, riding with Ple Two in his trump card Queen Mansa, he nearly wipes out the Gundam Team. But as he holds Ple Two back from Judau, Roux's Zeta Gundam snipes him.
A Neo Zeon officer. Aide to Mashymre and Chara, he flies mobile suits himself. Bemoaning his luck serving one odd commander after another, fretting over demotion,
he's a realist. But he has a ruthless side: on the moon he used Cecilia, childhood friend of Argama crewman Torres, to bomb the Argama. Ashamed of her weakness, Cecilia
acted, and his own bomb killed him.
A civilian boy from Shangri-La, a Side 1 colony. He supported himself and his sister Leina as a junk dealer. Trying to steal mobile suits
from the docked Argama, his sense of justice led him to drive off Yazan and Neo Zeon in the Zeta Gundam, and he became an Argama pilot. Full of drive and vitality, ever upbeat.
He fought for friends and Leina, but as they were drawn into war, he gained a clear will to fight to end it. Highly gifted as a Newtype,
he bonded with Haman and Ple. After beating Haman, he joins the Jupiter fleet with Roux to grow.
Ple's twin sister. More mind-controlled than Ple, and more aggressive. Fighting at Glemy's command, she kills Ple, but meeting Judau makes her
question her actions. In the final battle at Axis in the Queen Mansa, guided by Ple's soul, she finally leaves Glemy. But her body and mind were at their limit,
and after guiding Judau's escape from Haman's defeat, she dies.
A Neo Zeon officer. Chasing the Argama from Shangri-La, he sorties in mobile suits himself, but loses to Judau again and again. Utterly devoted to Haman,
he had the rose she gave him at a sortie coated as a treasure. Pulled from the front after many failures, he's made a Cyber-Newtype with his loyalty amplified.
His mind grows wildly unstable, and he dies fighting Rakan's unit of Glemy's faction, half out of control.
A battle-hardened Neo Zeon officer. A bold schemer so sure he can't be shot down he wears no normal suit. He sides with Glemy for rule of Earth once Glemy takes the Earth Sphere,
leading his Space Wolf Team to torment the Gundam Team. But in the final battle at Axis, the ZZ Gundam's High Mega Cannon wrecks his unit and he retreats.
Judau's sister. A kind girl who nagged Judau about his junk dealing but always worried for him. On the Argama she cooked and did laundry, until by chance Glemy took her in,
and she was schooled as a lady. When Neo Zeon took Dakar, she shielded Judau from Haman's shot and vanished in the fighting. But after all the battles ended,
Sayla Mass reunites her safely with Judau.
An AEUG volunteer who brought the ZZ's Core Fighter to the Argama. Her trademark: a shooting-star pilot suit. Once Judau took the ZZ, she became the Zeta Gundam's
pilot. Strong-willed and clear about her own will, she clashed with Judau's gang, who fought by chance, but slowly became their friend. Pursued one-sidedly by Glemy Toto,
she was baffled, but shed tears alone after shooting him at Axis. After the war, she joins the Jupiter fleet with Judau.
Leader of Londo Bell's mobile suits, rank Captain. In the One Year War he flew the RX-78 Gundam, set records, and proved to the Federation that Newtypes exist.
After the war, the Federation, fearing his power, kept him under house arrest. He later joined Karaba, the AEUG's backers, leading its mobile suits. After the First Neo Zeon War,
he joined Londo Bell, the Federation's independent unit, fighting nemesis Char's Neo Zeon and its plan to freeze Earth. Once a high-strung, needy boy, through those he met in war
and awakened as a Newtype, maturing greatly. In the Second Neo Zeon War he stopped Axis from falling to Earth, then vanished with Char and his own Nu Gundam.
A Neo Zeon Cyber-Newtype from Nanai's Newtype lab who flies the Jagd Doga. His parents died in the One Year War's colony drop, so he doesn't fully like Char's methods.
More stable than past Cyber-Newtypes, he's proud and hates being called one. Drawn to Quess, a true Newtype in his eyes, he stays near her to touch her power.
Secretly rivaling Char, he burns to beat Amuro, but Amuro shoots him down in the end.
Daughter of Federation Vice-Minister Adenauer Paraya. Fed up with her father and his mistress, she finds a place with Amuro on the Ra Cailum. But jealous of Chan,
she leaves for Char. Starved for love, she clings to Char, who needs her, and fights Londo Bell in the Alpha Azieru. She dies shielding Hathaway, who followed her to the battlefield.
Casval Rem Deikun, son of Zeon Zum Deikun, who dropped the name Quattro Bajeena, retook his One Year War alias Char Aznable, and became Neo Zeon's leader.
Why he doesn't use his real name, son of Zeon's founder, even as Neo Zeon's leader is unclear. After countless wars, to Earthnoids who still won't understand spacenoids,
he declares war on them.
A Federation tech officer who tunes the Nu Gundam. Fond of her superior Amuro, she throws herself into tuning the psycoframe to help him.
In the battle over Axis, hoping to help even a little, she sets out in a damaged Re-GZ to bring Amuro a psycoframe sample. Then, cutting between Hathaway and Quess,
she downs the Alpha Azieru, but Hathaway, enraged, shoots her dead.
Head of Neo Zeon's Newtype lab and also a tactical officer. Char's lover; rumor says that's how she got her post, but in fact she's a highly capable commander,
given full command once Char sorties. In private, too, she understood Char and tried to be his support.
Captain of the White Base in the One Year War, the Argama in the AEUG, and Londo Bell's flagship Ra Cailum. Decisive, with judgment born of vast combat experience.
A girl who died shielding Char from Amuro in the One Year War; the second Newtype sent into combat on purpose. She deeply moved both men; even dead, she still speaks to them.
A Neo Zeon pilot in a tuned blue Geara Doga. A veteran who despises Cyber-Newtypes and such powers. But Chan, her Newtype power briefly awakened by the psycoframe,
hit him square with her machine gun, and he died unable to believe he'd been shot down.
Supreme commander of the Crossbone Vanguard, aka Iron Mask. Left by his wife Nadia, ashamed of his weakness, he donned a mask, and to realize Meitzer Ronah's ideals
had his body enhanced: he can survive space unprotected, tear open mobile suit armor by hand, and steer machines by brainwave. He pushes the Rafflesia Project to cull mankind.
In the giant mobile armor Rafflesia he fights his daughter Cecily and Seabook, and is finally destroyed by the Gundam F91.
Young ace who leads the Black Vanguard, the Crossbone Vanguard's elite. As Berah Ronah's guardian he taught her to pilot, and her quick learning
made him believe in Newtypes. Devoted to Cosmo Aristocracy, he'd purge those ruled by emotion. But doubting Iron Mask, he's angered by the Bugs, which defy his creed.
He assassinates Carozzo's right hand Gillet Krueger, and lets the battered F91 that beat Carozzo go.
A civilian boy in the mechanics course at a Frontier IV high school. When the Crossbone Vanguard invaded Frontier IV, Dorel carried off his childhood friend Cecily before his eyes.
Fleeing the Crossbone fighting, he escaped the colony with friends to the Federation training ship Space Ark. There, as pilot of its new mobile suit F91, he begins
to fight the Crossbone Vanguard. A latent Newtype, he's highly attuned to the bio-computer his mother Monica built. Even amid fierce battle, he never forgets to protect his friends:
a kind-hearted boy.
A girl in the general course at Seabook's school. Really the eldest daughter of the Ronahs, who lead Cosmo Aristocracy: Berah Ronah. The Crossbone invasion takes her home.
Her grandfather Meitzer wants her as the Crossbone Vanguard's symbol, and she tries to live by his wishes, but persuaded by Seabook she chooses to cast off the Berah Ronah name.
Neo Sweden's Gundam Fighter, once a Lieutenant in its space forces. Trained from childhood at a base to be a Gundam Fighter. A combat genius using gymnastics-like moves.
A Neo Japan colony officer, rank Major. Leads the hunt for the Devil Gundam bound for Earth, backing Domon's team with sharp orders. Said to be an ex-Gundam Fighter...?
Domon's elder brother. With their father, he built the Ultimate Gundam to revive Earth, then stole it and fled once it was done. Why he did so remains unclear.
Or if it was even his own will...
Neo Germany's masked Gundam Fighter, a master of Germanic ninjutsu of untold power. He aids Domon, at times pushing him away; his identity is a mystery.
Domon's master, aka Master Asia. Neo Hong Kong's fighter and, in the original, last Gundam Fight's champion. Superhuman: he can take on mobile suits bare-handed.
He loves nature and humanity more than anyone, but his too-strong convictions lead him astray...
Neo Japan's Gundam Fighter, champion of colony martial arts with the title "King of Hearts." He can catch bullets bare-handed. Gruff and hard to approach,
but a fiery man, strong and kind.
Domon's childhood friend on the Neo Japan staff. She handles it all, from Gundam upkeep to caring for Domon. Bold as any man, she even pilots the Shining Gundam in his place.
She secretly loves Domon, but with him so oblivious and her so proud, she can't say it.
Rain's father, creator of the Shining Gundam. Invented a system linking human emotion to output. Dr. Kasshu's friend and rival; they built the Ultimate Gundam together.
Domon Kasshu's father, a Neo Japan scientist. Built the Ultimate Gundam with his son Kyoji. Accused of trying to misuse it and unleashing it on Earth as the Devil Gundam,
Neo Japan has him cryo-frozen.
An Earthling Drake summoned after Show and co. A US Air Force ace and Todd's senior. Cool, but sharp about his situation, he saw that the Earthlings in Byston Well
were really just mercenaries. Cunning too, he tried to use Drake's army in turn. His skill troubles Show and co., but in the battle of Rau he faces Show, now in the Billbine,
and is defeated.
A vassal of Rau. As captain of the aura ship Grimrey, he supplied Bochuns and more to Nie's group, and delivered the Billbine, entrusted by Queen Sheela of Na, to Show.
After King Foizon died he captained the Goraon as Ele's right hand, even punching the rash Show to teach him. Finally, holding Ele, who stopped the Black Knight going Hyper,
he rams the Goraon into the Gea Garing, his heart set on Byston Well.
A Mi Ferario serving Queen Sheela. Big sister to her companion Bell, she often teased her. Only Sheela's comforter, she never went to battle like Cham did,
but when first seen, she led Show to the captive Sheela.
Daughter of King Pinegan of Mi and granddaughter of King Foizon of Rau. After Foizon's death she commands the Goraon as Rau's princess, leading the fight against Drake.
Her unique aura, called spirit power, lets her foresee and sense evil auras. Yet she's a young girl; she wept over Tolstoll, an Earthling she loved, and Marvel and Keen
had to talk sense into her. As the war grew, she fulfilled her role as princess and purger of evil auras. In the finale, at the cost of her life, she absorbed the Black Knight's evil aura
and stopped him going Hyper.
Born to a knight's house in Ah, she ranks high among Drake's knights despite being a woman. Raised as a deserter's daughter, she craves glory and battle, and will stop at nothing.
She flies a Bastole tuned for her by Earthling engineer Zett Wright. Her amplified aura carried her to the surface with Show; there, she bonded with him, and they tried
to return to Byston Well together. But her aura was spent on the surface; her body couldn't survive the Aura Road, and she never returned to Byston Well.
A vassal of Na. As captain of the Gran Garan, he held real command in battle. A loyal retainer who worries for Sheela even in combat.
Daughter of the Kiss family, longtime Given retainers, ashamed her father Kibbutz sided with Drake to save the family. Devoted to Nie, who loves Rimuru, she acts rashly at times
to win his notice or to rival Rimuru. First the Wing Caliber Fou's pilot, she later flies an Aura Battler handed down by Marvel.
Burn Bunnings, after many defeats and blunders against Show Zama, cast off his past and donned a mask for revenge on Show. The war sparked by his raging aura summons Show.
Queen of Na. Called the holy maiden for her noble aura, she always bears a queen's dignity and grace. Out of duty she built the Gran Garan and leads the fight against Drake.
She saw Show, who saved her, as a true Holy Warrior and gave him the new Aura Battler Billbine. Grieving how aura machines changed Byston Well, her too, after Drake's fall
she resolved to scrap them all. On the surface she fought Drake while keeping chaos from spreading, even meeting the Queen of England. In the Pacific finale, she released her aura
to purify all evil auras and end the war.
An Earthling Drake summoned after Show and co. An Irish rock singer with streaked red hair. Aggressive, she treated the war in Byston Well like a game.
Back on the surface she went from Ireland to Greece, bending its military to her will with her aura. Leading air force jets in her Leprechaun, pilots called her
"the 20th-century Joan of Arc." But fighting Show and Marvel, her aura of rage and hate ran wild, causing the first-ever Hyper phenomenon. Her vast power cornered the Billbine,
but her runaway aura destroyed her.
A Japanese youth summoned to Byston Well for Drake via the Aura Road opened by the E Ferario Silky Mau. Adrift at first, meeting Marvel led him to join Drake's foes.
With his strong aura, he flies the Dunbine and Billbine at the heart of the anti-Drake forces, relied on as a Holy Warrior. A normal modern youth, he often felt awkward with it,
but as the war moved to the surface he grew into his role as a warrior and Nie's right hand. Hobbies: bikes and karate. He loved the big motorcycle summoned with him
to Byston Well, fretting over it early in Dunbine. To tell if it's really him, ask why rabbits' eyes are red: he answers, "Because they eat carrots."
An Earthling engineer summoned to Byston Well. Under Drake, he and Zett Wright fused robotics with aura power to create aura machines, while aiding Drake's
bid to conquer Byston Well. But secretly he meant to use Drake to become king; on the surface, in his own aura cruiser Spriggan, he acted apart from Drake.
As able a schemer as engineer, he evaded Drake's suspicion. In the finale his lover and aide Musie tried to kill Drake, but failed. At last, under Show and Marvel's attack,
he died with Musie.
A Mi Ferario allied with the Givens. At first sweet on Nie and wary of Show, then on Drake's side, she becomes his dear partner over time. In battle she shrieks orders at Show,
and shines at scouting and confusing foes. Handy at home, she made her own battle outfit late in Dunbine. Fairy-cute, she even got a figure made after appearing on the surface.
Dunbine is said to be the tale Cham, left alone on the surface after the last battle, told Earthlings. She's also the one who named the "Aura Slash."
An American summoned to Drake with Show. Practical and selfish, he sided with Drake even after Rimuru told him Drake's schemes, since Drake promised knighthood.
Beaten again and again by Show, his aura swelled with revenge. After vanishing, he returned as a knight of Ku, obsessed and troublesome. Yet his rivalry with Allen, love for his mother
and fixation on Show reveal a naive side. He flew a custom Dunbine, then a Drumlo, and after returning, the Bierres and Rineck. Just before the finale, his aura of hate for Show
explodes; his Rineck goes Hyper.
A provincial lord of Ah. With Earthling Shot Weapon he built aura machines, and summons Earthlings to conquer Byston Well. Shrewd and decisive, with strong aura power.
His ambition rests on a will that spurns even his daughter Rimuru's pleas. He overthrew his liege, King Fraon of Ah, finished the giant warship Wil Wiph, and began his conquest in earnest,
only to be sent to the surface with all the aura machines. Learning they grow stronger there, he spread his war to the surface. Amid Bishot's and Shot's plots and his wife Ruza's
infidelity, he fought Sheela and Ele; fleeing the Pacific finale, he fell to Nie, his ambition crushed.
Son of Romun Given, a lord of Ah. He fought with his father to stop Drake, but at first his feelings for his love Rimuru came first, and his spoiled willfulness often made him unreliable.
But he grew through battle; with duty and resolve he united the anti-Drake forces while leading a frontline strike team. After his ship Zelana sank before the finale,
he flew a Bochun and slew Drake in the final battle.
Captain of Drake's knights and a top Aura Battler pilot who also led the summoned Show and co. Once trusted by Drake, he lost his post after repeated failures. That humiliation
drove him to cast off pride and glory to hunt Show as his nemesis. Beaten time and again, he gave up even his name and face to live as the "Black Knight." His aura, swollen by hate,
troubled even Show's Billbine. On the surface, his vengeance kept powering him up until he went Hyper in the finale. Ele's sacrifice stopped it, but with an aura swollen by grudge
he challenged Show to one last fight.
An Earthling Drake summoned after Show and co., a Chinese self-styled "struggling actor." Pushy and glory-hungry, he joined Musie's attack. Show warned him,
of the risk in aiding Drake, but he ignored it, attacked, and was beaten.
A Mi Ferario serving Queen Sheela. Younger than Elle or Cham, she still looks and acts like a toddler. She asks honest, childish questions, and when big sister Elle mocks her,
she makes a fuss: the Gran Garan's mascot at Sheela's side.
An American woman summoned to Byston Well before Show by the E Ferario Knuckle Bee. Her family has a Texas ranch. Opposed to Drake and drawn to Nie, she aids the Givens.
She showed Show Drake's evil and won him over; she then accepted his love, and they raised each other's aura. A student of Eastern thought, rational yet given to fierce emotion.
She flew the newest anti-Drake Aura Battlers, the Dahna Ossie, Bozune and Bochun, then Show's Dunbine. Few solo feats, but as Show's partner she was a true Holy Warrior,
and her name is known across the anti-Drake side.
Drake's vassal, once Rimuru's music teacher. In love with Earthling Shot Weapon, she fought for him with her brothers Oll and Bibi and her father. Her aura, raised by love for Shot,
and fine aura machines like the Zwarth and Bubly trouble Show and co. As Shot's right hand, she tried to kill Drake for his ambition. In the final battle, Show and Marvel's attack
kills her along with Shot.
Drake's only daughter. In love with Nie of the enemy Givens, she fears Drake's ambition and secretly leaks his secrets. She ran away many times; once, Nie even
rescued her from Drake and she traveled with him. Sheltered but stubborn, she flew an Aura Battler rashly for Nie's approval. But she was taken back, and late in Dunbine
she was on Bishot's Gea Garing with her mother Ruza. She told Drake of Ruza's betrayal and set out to kill her mother, the root of the war.
Banjo's butler, a man of wholly unknown origin and past. A brilliant, ever-calm gentleman with keen tactical sense. A superb butler, he handles all, from Banjo's needs to intel
to mech upkeep, and even fights in Daitarn 3 himself. A gourmet who cooks like a top chef. A perfectionist: once, with Banjo in a pinch, he wouldn't launch Daitarn 3
because its waxing wasn't finished. His type: a sexy, mature, voluptuous beauty. He also enjoys melodramas.
A one-eyed commander ordered by Don Zauser to test an antigravity device. A typical Meganoid who sees humans as bugs. He floated a city to herd humans below like livestock.
Originally, a Banjo and Toppo goof left that city tilted 25 degrees left.
A commander who caught the newest mechs, made passengers Meganoids, and shrank the mechs into a miniature collection. Mad for fine new mechs, he even tried to shrink Daitarn 3.
Collecting was Benmel's own hobby.
A female Meganoid who put brainwave-control headbands on abducted humans to study the brain's potential. Very haughty. Perhaps for research, she made her subjects
build a pyramid that flies by human power. In the original she even controlled Reika, Beauty and Toppo, apart from Banjo, but Garrison destroyed her brainwave device.
Don Zauser's female Meganoid aide; the only one who can read the Don's will, she relays his orders. In the original, she fought Banjo in person.
An ex-Interpol cadet. She met Banjo while chasing a Meganoid and became his assistant. Thanks to Interpol, she's superb at shooting, fighting and piloting.
She and fellow assistant Beauty clash at times, but get along. Calm and ladylike at first glance, she's tough, and plays the fool with Beauty.
A boy whose parents were killed by Meganoids. He fought alongside Banjo's group and moved into Banjo's mansion. A self-styled first assistant, "hot-blooded" with "big dreams."
Super eager; he even stole Daitarn and flew it himself.
Leader of the Meganoids. Brain exposed and body plainly metal, he looks like an early model. He never speaks, plotting Meganoid rule of mankind through his aide Koros,
but no one knows if it's truly the Don's will or Koros's own.
Son of Sozo Haran, inventor of the Meganoids and Megaborgs. Hating his father, who sacrificed his brother and mother to experiments, and the Meganoids, years ago he took
Daitarn 3, a Meganoid prototype, and fled Mars. With the gold he took, he built a mansion near Shin the City. Now, with Beauty, Reika and co., he fights the Meganoids in Daitarn 3.
He handles all sorts of mechs and, with superhuman strength and marksmanship, is a strong fighter unaided. Smug and vain, utterly sure of himself with beautiful women,
but always humorous and a bit goofy: a charming man. Ruthless enough to abandon friends to beat the Meganoids, yet those around him
love and trust him all the more. The Haran Zaibatsu is original to this game.
Banjo's assistant. Daughter of a tour company president and a blonde beauty who won Miss International. A sheltered rich girl, carefree and still childish.
But when she snaps, she's a real fighter. Her love for Banjo is strong, so she and Reika feud constantly. Close to Toppo in mental age, she's his sparring partner too.
Actually a computer doll made by the Gaizok; the one attacking Earth is No. 8. Programmed to wipe out beings full of evil thoughts, after destroying Bial, the Jin family's ancestral home,
it slept for 200 years. Sensing evil thoughts filling modern humanity, it woke again and plots mankind's end through Butcher and others.
Bandock's commander, leading the Gaizok's extermination of mankind. Fat, huge, with a shrill voice, he looks comical but is utterly cruel and has no concept of life's worth.
His vile tricks took countless lives. As the name suggests, his design is modeled on a famous villain wrestler of old.
A 13-year-old who pilots the Zambo Ace and Zambot 3. Until the Gaizok came, he was a notorious brat, second son of a fishing boss in a Suruga Bay port town. Foreseeing the invasion,
his grandfather Hyozaemon gave him sleep-learning, making him pilot of the Zambo Ace and Zambot 3. Simple and overconfident, through many grim battles with the Gaizok he grew,
bonding with Uchuta, Keiko and kin.
A 15-year-old ninth grader who pilots the Zan Bull. The Kamie family are Tokyo doctors. At first he looked down on the younger, rough Kappei, but their friendship grew in battle,
and puts his cool intellect to use.
A 14-year-old eighth grader who drives the Zan Base. The Kamikitas run a ranch in Shinshu; Keiko is a skilled rider. Calm and strong-willed. As the Zan Base excels at scouting,
she mainly handles data in battle.
Kappei's grandfather, head of the Jin family. Preparing for the Gaizok, he dug up Zambot 3 and more, left by ancestors who fled Bial for Earth, and gave the kids
sleep-learning lessons in piloting and combat. He leads the family, guiding Kappei sternly but kindly.
Kappei's dog and partner. In the original he helps Kappei in everything from fights to battles. The Zambo Ace's seats are in its ankles; he usually rode in the right one.
When Chiyonishiki is aboard, he does the "Woof!" in the Zambot Combination call.
A cyborg Dr. Hell made from the mummies of a noble couple found in Bardos Island's ruins. Utterly loyal to Hell, riding the fortress Saluud or the Boodo, leading the Iron Mask Corps
and Mechanical Beasts at the front. Its staff controls them and fires a Destruction Ray, and it can transform. A cold schemer but sloppy, it loses to Mazinger Z time and again.
Yet Hell trusted it deeply; even cold Hell wept at its death.
Mazinger Z's pilot. Grandson of its maker Juzo Kabuto, son of Great Mazinger's maker Kenzo Kabuto. Heir to his grandfather's will after Baron Ashura killed him, he fought Dr. Hell.
After his grandfather died he moved to the Photon Power Lab with brother Shiro and entered Tojo Academy High. Hot-blooded and active, but easily carried away, he often rushed
into enemy traps. He's also soft-hearted and just, trusted by all. Superbly athletic and an expert biker. After defeating Dr. Hell,
he studied at NASA with Sayaka, but came home for the final battle with the Mykene Empire, riding Mazinger Z again alongside Great Mazinger.
An evil genius scientist bent on world conquest. German-born, expert in nuclear physics, engineering, cyborgs, archaeology, etc. A college classmate of Dr. Juzo Kabuto.
After college he built weapons for the military, then joined a dig on Bardos Island. Finding giant Mykene robots, he remade them as Mechanical Beasts to conquer the world. Ruthless,
he plagued Koji's team with raids, hostages and assassins. After his defeat, Mykene's Emperor of Darkness revived him as the Marshal of Hell to lead the Battle Beasts
after the Great General fell.
A brutal ex-German army officer reborn as a cyborg by Dr. Hell. His head, torn off by a bomb in his army days, acts apart from his body, floating by antigravity.
Sent to the front as strategist to end the losses to Mazinger Z. From the Flying Fortress Ghoul he leads his Iron Cross Corps and Mechanical Beasts. Cruel and proud,
he and Baron Ashura hate each other, always vying for credit. He serves Dr. Hell to the final battle on Hell Island and shares his fate.
Koji's classmate. Being sweet on Sayaka, he treats Koji as a rival in everything. To match Mazinger Z, he had the Photon Power Lab's three doctors build him his own robot,
Boss Borot, and fights with his flunkies Nuke and Mucha, though he's often a burden. Still, he's a big-hearted man of justice and Koji's irreplaceable best friend.
When Dr. Hell fell and Mykene invaded, he joined the Science Fortress Lab beside Great Mazinger. Like Nuke and Mucha, his real name is unknown (maybe Susumu Boda...).
Prof. Yumi's daughter, pilot of Aphrodite A and Dianan A. She skips high school to help her father's research at the Photon Power Lab. Strong-willed, she squabbles with Koji,
but inside she worries for him more than anyone. So she gets jealous of Koji's weakness for pretty girls, which can break their teamwork in battle. After defeating Dr. Hell,
she studied at NASA with Koji, but came home for the final battle with the Mykene Empire.
Full name Gennosuke Yumi. Juzo Kabuto's top student and director of the Photon Power Lab. He also built Aphrodite A and Dianan A, flown by his daughter Sayaka,
and upgraded Mazinger Z many times in the war with Dr. Hell. Gentle, calm and composed, with the sense of duty and judgment fit for the lab's director.
After Dr. Hell fell, he left the Mykene war to the Science Fortress Lab and returned to photon energy research.
A general of Mykene's foes, beaten by the Mykene ruler, the Emperor of Darkness, and revived as a humanoid Battle Beast. Now his loyal servant, he led the 7 Battle Beast armies
in conquering the surface. A brave warrior, he finally fell in a duel with Great Mazinger. His grieving men
showed how trusted he was: a true general. The movie "Mazinger Z vs. the Great General of Darkness" suggests a duel with Mazinger Z, yet the General himself
only makes a cameo (which, if anything, made him seem mightier).
A Mykene leader who appeared after the Great General fell to Great Mazinger: Dr. Hell, beaten by Mazinger Z and revived by Mykene power. Unlike the warlike
Great General, he prefers schemes.
Great Mazinger's pilot. Taken from an orphanage by Kenzo Kabuto at 7 to pilot Great Mazinger, a robot built for war, he underwent harsh training.
Raised as a combat pro, he's a strong fighter even unarmed. His past and cynical talk make him seem cold and hard to approach, but he's truly kind, and a stern man of justice.
He secretly loves Kenzo, who raised him, as a father, but is ashamed of being an orphan. So, jealous of Kenzo and Koji, home for the Mykene war, in the final battle
he made an irreparable mistake. Set at 22 when Great Mazinger began airing, he was later made 18, more youthful. In Gosaku Ota's manga,
he has a more comical side than on TV, yet is even harder-edged.
Venus A's pilot. Like Tetsuya, taken from an orphanage and harshly trained as a combat pro. Usually tough and competitive, but inside she's ashamed of her birth,
and sometimes broods alone.
Commander of the Earth invasion and of Skull Moon, the Vega Star Federation's base on the moon's far side. He holds two selves, man and woman; the woman is "Lady Gandal."
He looks male, but when Lady Gandal appears, her small body or face emerges on his. The two Gandals are separate and sometimes quarrel. As head of the invasion,
he fought Grendizer many times.
Once Vega's top genius girl scientist. She completed the Freeze Ray her late brother had researched. It was meant to cool young planets still too hot, but
King Vega saw its combat use and ordered her to kill Duke Fleed and seize Grendizer. In the original, she gets a chance to kill Duke on Earth, but in Maria shielding her brother
she sees herself.
An elite Vega Imperial Guard. In the original, as new commander he cornered Grendizer, but was betrayed and lost to Duke Fleed.
A skilled veteran of King Vega's guard. A whip master who can pull a glass to hand from meters away without spilling it. In the original, he saw that the 7.5 seconds to undock
and 6 to dock were its fatal "time of death," cornering Duke.
The Vega Star Federation's chief scientist, said to be Vega's top ladies' man. Known for his eyepatch, finned helmet and yellow one-piece. He designed many saucer beasts,
fighting Grendizer with Commander Gandal. They seem to be rivals, but team up when needed. In the original he has a son, Zuril Jr.
Daisuke Umon's true self: prince of Fleed, destroyed by the Vega Star Federation. When Vega struck, he fled in Grendizer to Earth. He makes lush Earth his second home,
loving it and its people from the heart. When Fleed was attacked, he saved a friend in peril and took a lasting Vegatron radiation wound in his right arm. A kind, sincere youth, but
only the Vega Star Federation knows how terrible his anger is.
King of Vega, home of the Vega Star Federation. His flagship is a giant UFO, the King of Vega. As Vegatron radiation brought Vega near ruin, he sought a new world
and set his sights on Earth. Cruel and ruthless, but soft on his daughter Rubina.
Duke Fleed's sister, a tomboy with unstable precognition. When Vega attacked Fleed, she was separated from her brother, and a Fleed elder, later her foster parent,
got her to Earth. In the original, told she was Fleed's princess but unaware her brother lived, she thought Vega had taken Grendizer and hunted Duke.
She has a crush on Koji Kabuto.
Dr. Umon's adopted son, a hand at Shirakaba Ranch: Duke Fleed in disguise. Likes guitar and long rides. Serious and reliable; even rough Koji Kabuto speaks politely to him.
Crying "Duke Fleed!", he transforms into Duke Fleed.
Full name Genzo Umon. Daisuke's foster father and head of the Space Science Laboratory, a quiet man who watches over him as Earthling and prince. When Duke Fleed fled
to Earth, he adopted and raised him; once the Vega war began, he remade the lab for Grendizer to aid Duke.
Main pilot of America's Texas Mack and son of its developer, Dr. King. Proud and cocky, he called the Getter Team "three halves of a pilot."
Backed by skill, he beat Getter Robo in a mock fight. But Getter-3 saved him from a Mechasaur, and they came to respect each other.
Jack's sister, pilot of the hat-shaped machine that supports and arms Texas Mack. Polite, she smooths over Jack's aggressive behavior, and backs him up well in battle.
Pilot of the Eagle/Getter-1 and Dragon/Getter Dragon. Captain of Asama Academy's soccer team, he replaced Dr. Saotome's son Tatsuto, killed by the Dinosaur Empire,
he fights as a Getter Robo pilot. Earnest, single-minded, with a strong sense of duty, if a bit rigid, he united the Getter Team as leader. His family runs a kendo dojo in Kyushu, and he
knows swordplay and uses it in battle. He rides a sidecar bike.
Pilots the Jaguar/Getter-2 and Liger/Getter Liger. When the Dinosaur Empire struck, he refused classmate Ryoma's plea, but with Michiru, like his late mother, in peril,
he volunteered to pilot. A cool, athletic nihilist and deep thinker, he's easily misread and clashed at times with hotheads Ryoma and Musashi. Yet he burns quietly with purpose,
bound deeply to his comrades at heart. Hobby: harmonica.
Pilots the Poseidon and Getter Poseidon. A new student at Asama Academy, he met Dr. Saotome's son Genki; his great strength got him scouted for the Poseidon.
He refused at first, but regretting Genki's injury in a Hyakki attack, he joined the fight. Easygoing and peace-loving by nature, he's gentle with animals and kids.
He loves baseball and later captains Asama Academy's team. In the original, he never uses Musashi's Daisetsuzan Oroshi.
A Hyakki Empire leader on par with Dr. Gula; in effect, its field commander. A total coward, servile to the powerful, merciless to the weak, whose plans often use hostages.
In the original he even interfered with Tekkouki's duel with Getter Robo, a coward to the end.
The emperor atop the Hyakki Empire. Bold, fond of flashy tactics, but coldly uses dirty tricks when needed. Seeking to turn all humans into oni or wipe them out,
he fights the Getters in his way.
Head of the Saotome Lab. Losing eldest son Tatsuto in the Dinosaur Empire's first attack left wife Kazuko, daughter Michiru and son Genki. A top Getter ray scientist, he
built Getter Robo for space development, but armed it to fight the Dinosaur Empire, and later completed a new combat Getter Robo. Stubbled and in geta, he looks shabby,
but he's not just a top scientist: in battle he leads the Getter Team with cool judgment and precise orders. Mild-mannered, he'll still yell to stop his three hotheads.
Leader of the Combattler team, pilot of unit 1, the Battle Jet. Orphaned in an accident, he was taken in by the Taiyo Academy orphanage. A skilled biker, quick to fight,
fierce-tempered, and a born genius in combat. Shot through the arm in a fight with Garuda, he got a high-tech prosthetic. Cheerful and simple, he "crushes the strong, helps the weak,"
to a tee, and never gives up in a pinch. But he's hopeless with girls, slow to respond to Chizuru's advances.
Combattler team member, pilot of unit 2, the Battle Crusher. Cynical, cool and foul-mouthed, but his Kansai dialect softens it. He sometimes argues with Hyoma,
even trading punches, but at heart they accept each other as comrades. A genius marksman who won a contest at 8, his aim has saved the team many times.
Combattler team member, pilot of unit 3, the Battle Tank. Laid-back: the gentle-giant type. From Kyushu, he wants to be a manga artist,
and is a judo master too.
The Combattler team's only girl, piloting unit 4, the Battle Marine. Its idol, granddaughter of Combattler V's maker Dr. Nanbara. A whiz at oceanography, medicine, robotics,
she's also good at piano, swimming and gymnastics. Kind but tomboyish. She loves Hyoma and once shielded him, but usually can't be honest, so they made little progress.
The Combattler team's youngest, pilot of unit 5, the Battle Craft. A grade-school genius who studied at a US college, he's made many great (and odd?) inventions.
Yet he's still a kid, losing his cool when his parents' home in Hokkaido became an enemy target. His weakness: he wets the bed.
Campbell's commander for the Earth invasion: a giant stone statue, really a computer holding Campbellian scientist Oleana's mind. It taught the android Garuda it was his mother
and made him swear total loyalty. It forced Combattler V apart with the Narumagne Ray when it stormed the secret base, but Garuda, learning he'd been fed lies, turned on it in rage,
attacking with the Big Garuda.
The Campbellians' battle commander, who becomes a birdman in battle or rage. He fought on orders from his mother Oleana, head of the invasion, to remake Earth for Campbellians.
Proud, he saw Combattler V and Hyoma as his nemeses. But learning he was an elaborate android made by Oleana, he raged at her lies and, in the Big Garuda,
rebelled. After defeating Oleana, he challenged Combattler V to a final duel for his pride.
Campbell's empress. In the original, after Oleana's fall, she came to invade Earth with the brothers Warukimedes and Dangel. Beautiful, but cold and ruthless,
unforgiving of failure. When she shows her true self, her face turns hideous, likely its real form.
In the original, after Oleana's fall he came with Empress Janera and his brother Warukimedes as Campbell's new general. Huge and muscled, with a claw for a left arm: a born brawler,
he flew Magma Beasts at Combattler.
A giant riding the sky in a two-horse chariot, envoy of Campbell's peace faction. In the original's finale, he stopped the Earth Bomb Janera set off as she died, saving Earth.
Garuda's halfroid aide, her lower body part of a wall. Runs the Campbell rest area, mainly soothing a weary Garuda with song and music. Though an android, she has feelings,
and out of love for Garuda risks her life to beat Combattler V.
In the original, one of Empress Janera's men who came after Oleana's fall; elder brother of General Dangel. A brilliant mind, he develops Magma Beasts and plans operations,
aiding Janera's invasion. Cautious, so Janera and Dangel call him a coward.
A scientist who heads the Nanbara Connection after his old friend Dr. Nanbara died. When Nanbara first called him there to lead the Combattler team,
he refused, bitterly wishing mankind would perish. But when Nanbara gave his life to save him, he resolved to fight for the nature he loves. Bold and foul-mouthed, yet in any crisis
he never quits seeking a way out. He loves liquor and always carries a whiskey bottle.
A brainwave robot Dr. Nanbara made for combining. It reads the five pilots' brainwaves; only when the meters on its body align, proving their brainwaves in sync,
can they combine. In short, without Ropet, there's no combining. It has human-like feelings and once fell in love with a pretty
robot girl sent by the enemy.
Younger Kyoretsu brother, a demon officer under Barao. Brutish and hot-tempered, he fights Raideen.
The elder Kyoretsu brother, a demon officer under Demon Emperor Barao. Dressed like an admiral, he's calmer than his brother. They feud, but in the original he raged at Gekido's death,
so he must have cared after all.
Leader of the Copelander Team, the Future Engineering Lab's combat unit, called "Mister." He flies the Bluegar to back Raideen. Cool and a bit cynical, he clashed with rash Akira,
but they became best friends. Before the final battle with the Demon Empire, he died ramming the enemy.
A Copelander Team member with precognition who can hear Raideen's inner voice, so only she can give Akira and co. certain advice. Wise and calm, unlike Mari,
who always suspected her and Akira. Once, seeking purpose, she ran with a biker gang.
Akira's classmate, Rinkai Academy's idol, daughter of Future Engineering Lab director Higashiyama. Cheery and tomboyish; Akira teases her clumsiness. His support, at last,
eager to help, she joins the Copelander Team to back Raideen.
Great Demon Emperor of the Demon Empire, who once sank Mu and now plots a Demon Century on the surface. He's a giant statue in the empire's temple, and through it
he gives orders to Sharkin and others, revives fossil beasts and punishes his men. When Sharkin falls, he emerges in true form to invade the surface with the Kyoretsu brothers.
Captain of Rinkai Academy's soccer team, an athletic boy. Destined to merge (Fade In) with Raideen, the legacy of King Ra Mu. To stop the Demon Century,
he fights the Demon Empire in Raideen. A cheerful, hot-blooded hero, with strength unbowed by fate and courage undaunted by despair.
Prince of the Demon Empire. Noble and honorable, yet as its prince, a cold man who'll use any means. He once came to Akira disguised as a human
transfer student, under the name Kingo Sunaba.
Director of the Future Engineering Lab and Mari Sakurano's father. Against the Demon Empire he built the science fortress Mutropolis; while commanding it, to back up Raideen,
he formed the Copelander Team.
Akira's father, an archaeologist. In the original, in episode 1, demons turned him and his ship to stone; later Sharkin took him.
Akira's missing mother; really Princess Lemuria of ancient Mu. She slept 12,000 years to stop Demon Emperor Barao's revival. Waking today, she married Ichiro Hibiki,
bore Akira, then vanished to seek Mu's treasure, the Star of Ra Mu.
22, Japanese. Quiet and reserved, he seems cool and calm but burns quietly within. Slow to speak his mind, he's often misunderstood, but doesn't care.
A gambler who loves long odds. He fights the same way, making reckless charges in Alteisen, a heavy assault Personal Trooper built only for close combat. Curt, but he
cares deeply for partner Excellen.
23, American. Calm and smart at heart, but her showy, flippant talk keeps people from seeing it. (She doesn't much mind.)
The team's mood-maker, for better or worse: a cheery big sister. Ever at her own pace; a heavy drinker. She races into battle in Weissritter, a high-mobility Personal Trooper.
Kyosuke's lover. But her opposite, Kyosuke, is so curt that it's a sore point. (She wants a burning romance.)
The only humanlike member of the mysterious enemy "Einst series." She seems concerned with Kyosuke, though they've never met. Her looks and voice resemble Excellen's,
so she must be linked to Kyosuke and Excellen somehow...
A being shrouded in mystery. "The Land of Beginning," "correction," "a new universe"... These keywords will reveal what it is and its terrible goal.
A giant warship 1.4 km long, 600 m high. Built under the Cyber Beast Force base, it launched as the base fell. Its main Gandoll Cannon's principle is used in the Danku Sword.
Armed also with lasers and Vulcans, it's truly a great dragon of the skies. But its three fusion reactors can only run for 183 days from startup.
The ultimate form of Dr. Kotaro Hazuki's four Cyber Beasts, combined. Debuts in episode 16, "Beyond Beast, Beyond Man, Arise Divine Warrior (2)." Main pilot: Shinobu Fujiwara.
Its kanji mean "I become the sky and sever worldly desires." Controlling it takes huge willpower, so the Cyber Beast Force mastered each mode in turn until they reached a set level
its combination code stayed sealed. Hugely powerful, it fought almost only in melee at first. Later the Danku Sword, Daigun and more were added, and to fix its lack of flight,
a flight booster was built. As new foes came, it and its dragon mothership Gandor were upgraded often. The Danku Koga Sword is from the OVA; it's used by channeling
Gandor's power to the Danku Sword.
The original's mech of Guildrome, Muge general of the Mystery Corps.
A Muge Empire mech from the movie that rampages with its huge body and Flame. It has a self-destruct; in the original it blew away a city.
In the original, the mech of Death Gaiyer, one of Muge's 3 generals. Regeneration, missile swarms and Dissolving Fluid plagued Dancougar. In his colosseum "Red Space"
it faced Dancougar, and lost.
As the name says, Shapiro Keats's mech, with a strong Beam Cannon. In the original its right shoulder trembled, like Shapiro's piloting habit.
A giant inside planet Dirad: really just a branch of a huge tree living in the planet. It fights with strength and vines from its body, and since its power is Dirad's own,
it regenerates from any attack. In the original its planetary power hurt the Cyber Beast Force, but Shinobu found its weakness via the Eagle Fighter and cleaved it and its tree.
A mass-produced Muge robot. Weak, but comes in numbers.
A humanoid mech deployed by Dirad. Relies on numbers. Its main weapon is a shoulder Beam Cannon.
In the original, Keim's mech, Dirad's trump card. It cornered Dancougar without Masato, but the dying Shapiro took his seat and unleashed wild power; the Danku Sword cut it
down along with Dirad's core.
A fake Dancougar by Muge Zorbados: wingless, with birdlike ankles. In the original it trades punches with Dancougar and crumbles.
Muge Zorbados himself.
A mid-size robot Rom summons with Kenrou. Nimble fighter.
A giant robot summoned by Kenrou. Unlike Kenryu, it's built for one-hit kills. Just plain strong!
A bull robot formed by Kina and Colon, children of bison warrior Jingi. Uses tackles and shocks like their father's. In the original it wraps its tail to shock, but God Hand Final rips it off,
and a Fire Chop snaps its horn.
Triple Jim himself. No built-in weapons; he uses handhelds like a Bazooka.
Triple Jim's helicopter mode.
Triple Jim's car mode. In the original, he usually traveled this way with Leina aboard.
Powered armor; only 3 appear, just before the original's finale. Its limbs follow the wearer's. Rom used it for Tenku Chushin Ken moves.
Blue Jet himself. His only built-in weapon is a hip sword for Tenku Shinken secrets. The Blazer Cannon, added mid-series, shares its name with Rod Drill's, but
Jet's cannon fires beams.
Blue Jet's flight mode. No sword, but it gains a built-in Vulcan and Blazer Cannon. In the original it even carried Rom hanging below.
Rod Drill himself. No built-in weapons, and his trademark drill can't be used in this mode, so he fights with fists. In the original he had no real special move, just punches and throws.
His Blazer Cannon's muzzle differs from Jet's: it's a Missile Launcher.
Rod Drill's drill tank mode. More arms than in humanoid form, like drill charges and Vulcans; it can burrow.
A Demon Commander with a body of iron sand. It has its own will, yet oddly can carry a rider; Bug Newman rode it. With Electromagnetic Irradiation, Double Sword and more,
armed for any range, but in the original, Bug lost because he couldn't use his "EM Poison Hand."
Gades himself, the Gyandlar's boss. Fires many fireballs and slashes with a sword that warps to him. His left arm with a giant shoulder claw skewered Blue Jet in the original.
Gardy himself. No built-in weapons; he fights only with Nagase, the twin sword to Kenrou. Who is he really...?
Casmodon himself, a low-ranking Gyandlar Demon Commander. After a grand debut in episode 11 and a loss to the Thunder Claw, it reappeared en masse, maybe mass-produced.
Grujios himself. His body is just for show; the real him is the grub-like face floating in the tank on his face.
Glowbine himself. His only weapons are two swords on his back. The Dark Twin Slayer Sword, somehow, splits him fully in two.
Zarios himself, a low-ranking Gyandlar Demon Commander, notable for his caterpillar-tread legs.
Diondra herself. She wields an Electromagnetic Whip and Medusa, a cursed sword that drives its holder mad, and breathes fire. In the original, her Eye Flash hypnotized foes.
Devil Saturn No. 1-6 combined. Besides melee it has many attacks: mouth Flame, chained claws, eye beams and more. In the original it also shot Tentacles from its chest,
retracted its head to spew Dissolving Fluid: too many attacks!
Falgos himself, a low-ranking Gyandlar Demon Commander. Known for agility, though the original barely showed it.
Mizuchi himself; really a mass-produced copy from Grujios's sorcery and Gyandlar revival tech. Uses the Dragon King Sword and kicks like the Water Dragon Kick.
Built by Dr. Tarsan for Grand Captain Garimos, who wanted the strongest robot. Four fighters, the "Dan Mechanics," combine into Dangaioh. Its pilots are all psychics,
and their powers drive its power. It has super robot moves like Boost Knuckle and Dangai Beam, and hero-show moves like "Psychic Slash," fusing sword and psychic power.
In the final battle with Gil Gear, it blows up, leaving only the cockpit.
A giant golden robot flown by Shazara to destroy Dangaioh. In the original, the fighters of Shazara and her partners Domdon and Oscar combine into it.
Uses the spear-hand "Iron Crusher" and "Plasma Typhoon," gathering air energy in its back spikes to fire from its hands. Pinned by the Psychic Wave, it falls to the Spiral Knuckle
Lamba fires through her tears.
A blue, one-legged freak robot flown by Burst, fighting with that leg. In the original it took on Dangaioh with Raidoll, but fell to Roll's fury.
A red, knightlike robot flown by Flash, armed with a lance-sword hybrid and a big shield. In the original it took on Dangaioh with Blast, and the Psychic Wave crushed both at once.
Grand Captain Garimos himself. He keeps a noisy space creature called the "Jester" on his shoulder.
Gil Berg's mech after his revival as a cyborg: his own unit, as named. In the original it overwhelmed Dangaioh and nearly won, but Roll and co.'s last-ditch
Psychic Wave wrecked it.
Flown by Tarsan's men Yold and Dira. In the original they chased the fleeing Dangaioh team, and Pai's strength hurled boulders at them. Its top weapon can burn a 10 km radius:
the "Hyper Napalm."
A giant mech Garimos gave Gil to chase Dangaioh; also called "Bloody." It fights with size and power. Its head holds Bloody II, which can launch and redock at will.
Psychic Slash cleaves it in two.
A humanoid robot stored in Bloody I's head. Fast, it pierces foes with its arm's Blood Sword. In the original it cornered Dangaioh, but Roll's plan to let it pierce their chest and pin it
cost it an arm.
A ship with a phase transition engine, built by Nergal Heavy Industries. With a Gravity Blast and Distortion Field, it can travel in air, sea and space. Its gravity wave beam for the Aestivalis
