The Nadesico force-fitted with the Y Unit meant for the 4th Nadesico-class ship Shakuyaku ("Y Nadesico"). It can fire the Phase Transition Cannon, shifting a whole area.

Superior Human Corps flagship of commander Kusakabe.

A ship of mysteries: its machines answer only to legendary ninja, and Tobikage always appears near it.
One of the Elshank's three machines. Like the others, only one of ninja blood can pilot it; mainly Joe Maya. Besides a Gatling Launcher and Beam Gun from its chest's lion head,
it has ninja weapons like a sword and Shuriken bombs. It combines with Tobikage to form Beast Demon.
A golden lion: Tobikage combined with Kurojishi. Kurojishi may have picked Joe for how his wild nature suits Beast Demon. Besides lion-style melee like Bite,
it has many weapons, like horn beams and mane heat rays. In the original it formed 7 times, the most of the three machines.
A Za Boom Army battle robot; in the original, a unique commander's unit. Agile despite its size, with a huge sword, trident and Shuriken: the best of the Bancs and Sherman in one.
In the original, it slowly spun its spear to hypnotize Joe.
As strong as Tobikage, piloted by Ilbora in his rivalry with Joe. Armed much like Tobikage, but with differences such as dual swords. It seems linked to the "ninja legend"...
A mysterious ninja robot that appears from nowhere to save Joe and co. Small but blazing fast, it overwhelms foes with a Beam Bowgun, ninja sword, Makibishi Launcher and more.
It combines with Kurojishi, Houraiou and Blast Dragon as the core of Beast, Sky and Sea Demon. Likely most tied to the "ninja legend"...?
An Elshank robot flown by Mike Coil. It has a Pole Axe, but excels at range with shoulder cannons and light-wave shells. Combines with Tobikage into Sea Demon.
A blue bipedal dragon: Tobikage plus Blast Dragon. Same cannons and shells, plus mouth Flame and lightning. Strong at any range, but in the original it formed only twice,
losing to Zerokage the second time.
An Elshank machine flown by Lenny Ai. Its Cross Sword folds and joins into a Lance or Boomerang. Of the three machines, the best at air and high-mobility combat.
Combines with Tobikage: Sky Demon.
Houraiou and Tobikage combined: a giant crimson hawk. It has a Beam Cannon, but mostly sweeps foes away with flaming charges. In the original it formed one time fewer than Kurojishi:
6 times. It was most used when battles were in space.
A small Za Boom robot with scythes and Needle Missiles. In the original it made clones, posed as walls and burrowed, ninja-style.
A mid-size Za Boom Army battle robot shaped like a ronin samurai, mainly using a sword and trident. It breathes fire and fires palm missiles: a well-rounded attacker.
A long-range type: a Bancs with a long-range gun on one arm. In the original, mounted only on the outer walls of the giant fortress Excellent.
Mars base Commander Hazard Pasha's ship. In the original's finale it fell easily to Sky Demon.
A general-purpose mobile suit made in Operation V by the Federation, far behind Zeon in MS tech. It far outclassed the Zaku; even novice Amuro downed 2 Zaku in its debut.
The first MS-size handheld mega particle gun, solo reentry, the Core Block System, arms for all ranges, a learning computer, new armor: its many features
shaped later mobile suits. With Amuro's rising Newtype power it won big; Zeon feared "the Federation's White Devil," "White Meteor," "the White One." But late in the original,
the machine couldn't keep up with Amuro's Newtype powers; magnetic coating improved its response. After the One Year War, many mobile suits bore its name, and it became a legend.
A Core Fighter with a large booster for more range and firepower. Armed with a Mega Particle Cannon, it can handle mobile suits too. The White Base had two:
Sayla's and Sleggar's.
The Federation's third One Year War Gundam, refitted on the moon as a magnetic coating testbed. Its response is improved, but there's no record of Amuro Ray ever piloting it.
In the novels, though, it's the last unit Amuro rode. The prototype Gundam's model number is RX-78-1, the White Base unit's is RX-78-2, and this unit's is
RX-78-3, hence the nickname "G-3 Gundam" (or it was a radio code name). Some say Amuro switched to the G-3 in the TV series when the Gundam was coated at Solomon,
but this is uncertain.
Strictly, this isn't the MS-06S Zaku II flown by Char Aznable, the "Red Comet," but an MS-06FZ Zaku II Kai painted red. So it doesn't exist in the original or official Gundam history.
A Zeon mobile suit of the One Year War: a Zaku II redesigned for ground use. With a Machine Gun on the left and its signature Heat Rod electric whip on the right, it excels up close.
Ramba Ral's unit gave Amuro's Gundam a hard time. Later mass-produced, many were sent into battles like the Jaburo assault.
A big space battleship of Zeon's Zabi family in the One Year War. Three were built, the first being Sovereign Degwin Zabi's Great Degwin. Strong in firepower and MS capacity,
it's a fierce warship. Just in case, it could also reach the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter. In fact, Char Aznable left for Axis in a Gwazine-class,
as seen in the ending of the movie "Encounters in Space."
A mobile cruiser Zeon built in the One Year War. It can reenter alone, fly in atmosphere on its lifting body, and leave it with boosters. In the original, Ramba Ral and Char
used it as a mothership.
Zeon's first amphibious MS. A masterpiece with built-in mega particle cannons, heavy armor, and agility in water and on land. Its catch of a Hyper Hammer in the original
is very famous.
Zeon's super-large space transport carrier. It held 182 mobile suits and could launch 7 at once by catapult. Heavily armed too, it was a core of the front lines.
A heavy space mobile armor Zeon built in the One Year War. With many high-output mega particle cannons and an I-field anti-beam barrier, it's a fearsome fighter.
But due to cooling issues, it could fight at full power under 20 minutes. Its legs can be detached in emergencies. As Dozle's trump card for defending Solomon,
it was sent into battle, fighting Sleggar's G-Fighter (Core Booster in the movies) and Amuro's Gundam. Had it been mass-produced, it would have been used to invade Jaburo,
the Federation's HQ.
A wrecked Ground Gundam rebuilt with extra armor. It has many options solely for ground combat and can carry a Container on its back. Its name is short for
"Extra Zero 8."
A mobile armor for assaulting bases, developed by Ginias Sahalin. It flies by Minovsky craft, armed only with a Large Mega Particle Cannon. Meant to drop from space to attack and
seize bases, but the brass found it "far too unrealistic."
A custom Gouf. It drops built-in arms for a wire Heat Rod and Gatling Shield, improving versatility and range. But only skilled pilots can handle it,
so few were deployed.
The final base-assault mobile armor, built from Apsaras prototype 1 and 2 data. Bigger, with stable flight and firepower, but poor in safety and durability.
In the original, an Ez-8 punch to the cockpit just above its cannon port brings it down.
A Newtype Gundam built by the Federation late in the One Year War; the 4th Gundam, formally the RX-78-NT1 Gundam Alex. "Alex" comes from
its "RX" model code. Unlike Zeon's Newtype units it has no psycommu; it only improves response with magnetic coating.
The first unit with a panoramic monitor, it can wear Chobham Armor, whose built-in charges cancel outside impacts. Meant for the White Base unit,
it fought on Side 6 with its tuner Chris as pilot. It traded blows with Bernie's Zaku II Kai, and never reached Amuro.
Zeon's last mass-produced mobile suit of the One Year War. An assault type, its thrusters all over give it agility far beyond earlier mobile suits.
Its flaw: that agility burns propellant fast, so its operating time is short. Its missions call for many weapons all over its body, mostly live ammo,
meant to be dumped when spent before withdrawing. In the original, Steiner's Cyclops Team used it on Side 6 to steal the NT-1 Alex.
Properly, the Zaku II Kai: Zeon's improved Zaku II from the end of the One Year War. Other mobile suits moved to second-run models under the Unified Maintenance Project,
such as the Rick Dom II. Its thrust is 70% above the Zaku II's, but with the same propellant, its operating time is halved.
Arms were upgraded too, with Hand Grenades as standard.
The final mass-produced Gelgoog, the Gelgoog Jager. High-performance but very few were built. Its precise beam rifle earns it the alias "sniper Gelgoog."
An amphibious MS from the end of the One Year War. With stretchable arms for close combat and built-in beam cannons, it's based on the Gogg, but really
the peak of Zeon's amphibious MS.
A light cruiser of the Zeon Republic forces (later absorbed by Neo Zeon). An upgraded Musai, Zeon's One Year War mainstay, but with only exterior changes, there's
little real improvement.
An Anaheim Electronics mobile suit. Though a Gundam prototype candidate, it was built mainly by ex-Zeon engineers, so it looks nothing like a Gundam.
Meant to be Gundam GP04, it fell to the Delaz Fleet and is flown by Cima Garahau.
A Gundam prototype built mainly by Anaheim Electronics after the One Year War at the Federation's request. Made for gravity, it's designed
to move more like a human. It inherits the RX-78 Gundam's concept, with a Core Block System. Code name Zephyranthes (rain lily), whose flower means "pure love."
Called the Full Vernian: Gundam GP01 refit for space. The frame is nearly unchanged, but added thrusters and propellant tanks greatly boost its space mobility and
operating time.
Like GP01, a Gundam prototype built by Anaheim Electronics at the Federation's request. Made to use tactical nukes, it has an Atomic Bazooka that fires
a Mk82 nuclear warhead. Built to return from ground zero, it has thorough heat and shock proofing, and its big shield has a cooling unit.
Anavel Gato of the Zeon remnant Delaz Fleet stole it from the Federation's Torrington base. Code name Physalis (ground cherry), whose flower means "deceit."
Like GP01 and GP02, built by Anaheim Electronics at the Federation's request, for base defense. Its concept: a weapon with both a mobile suit's versatility and
a mobile armor's speed and firepower. It's formed by the mobile suit unit Gundam Stamen and
the Orchis armed base holding its weapons. It also has an I-field generator for beam defense. Code name Dendrobium (an orchid), whose flower means "selfish beauty."
The mobile suit unit of the Gundam GP03, built by Anaheim Electronics. A space combat unit, strong on its own, but designed to dock with the Orchis armed base.
So it has special gear like folding support arms to pull weapons from containers and hip tail binders. "Stamen" is a flower's pollen organ.
A postwar GM-line suit the Federation built to upgrade its mass-produced units. A better generator and apogee motors boost its mobility. Descended from the NT-1 Alex,
and went mainly to aces. Per Kou, its trait is having no traits.
A mid-range support mobile suit the Federation built after the One Year War using RX-77D Guncannon data. Its shoulder cannons fire beams, and it has a Beam Saber for close combat.
Its armor seems modeled on the NT-1 Alex's Chobham Armor.
A large prototype space mobile armor built by the Zeon remnants at Axis after the One Year War, given to the Delaz Fleet, their partners, for Operation Stardust.
Huge beam weapons all over give it massive firepower and speed, plus an I-field generator and wired all-range attacks.
A prototype mobile armor Zeon was building at Granada late in the war. Ex-Zeon soldier Kelly, who lost an arm, hid it in his moon factory and finished it. Before it went to Cima,
Kelly chose to fight Kou's Gundam GP01Fb in it on the moon. Its signature weapon is the plasma leader.
A version of the MS-14 Gelgoog called the Gelgoog Marine, descended from the high-mobility Gelgoog of the war's end. Weaker than the Gelgoog J, but
cheaper to build. Mainly used by Cima's fleet; Cima's commander unit has extra mobility and weapons.
A Zeon prototype heavy mobile suit from the end of the One Year War. It has a folding 68cm Cannon for long-range shelling, and hovers faster than it looks.
Also called "Merza un Kanone."
Read "Rick Dom Zwei." The Rick Dom's second-run model under Zeon's Unified Maintenance Project at the end of the One Year War. Improved, it later became the basis
of Neo Zeon's mobile suit Dreissen. Many variants exist for different fronts.
A general-purpose Titans mobile suit, a redesign of the One Year War's RX-78 Gundam by mainly Earth-born engineers. Due to armor issues and such, only 3 prototypes were
built, but its movable frame, splitting armor from internals, shaped later MS design (especially mass production). Testing at Gryps 2, it was seized by the AEUG's
Quattro Bajeena and Kamille Bidan, then held by MPs, and repainted on the Argama. Then, with Kamille as pilot, it won great victories, as in the Jaburo assault,
and more. Later, Kamille's idea of Flying Armor for reentry enabled fast ground combat (though it was only used at Jaburo...).
After Kamille moved to the Zeta Gundam, Emma flew it, and in Gundam ZZ it was mostly Elle Vianno.
The Titans' successor to the RX-78 Gundam. Made for combat inside colonies but highly versatile. Painted in Titans colors (black and navy), starting with the GM Quel.
Built to be the Titans' symbol, but its designer, Franklin Bidan, saw it as a mere stepping stone. Three were built, and all of them
fell into AEUG hands.
MS mode of a Federation transforming mobile armor. Noted for binders on both arms with built-in mega particle cannons, which are also active thrusters,
giving it amazing mobility.
A Federation transforming mobile armor. Built for space, it uses a big booster for long trips. Its acceleration is so brutal that only a few, like Yazan and Cyber-Newtype Rosamia,
were issued one. Its flaw: a blind spot under its panoramic monitor. Docked, its legs serve as landing gear.
A Newtype mobile suit built at the Federation's Murasame Lab. It looks like a Gundam, but its design is based on Zeon's Zeong. It has no psycommu weapons,
but psycommu controls run the beam cannons all over its body. Poor mobility, but its armor and firepower crush normal mobile suits. Its pilot, Murasame Lab Cyber-Newtype
Four Murasame, faces Kamille in Hong Kong and Kilimanjaro.
The Psyco Gundam's mobile armor mode, mainly for cruising, as only this mode can use Minovsky craft. But unlike other mobile armors, it gains little mobility.
Too huge to fit in the Garuda-class transport Sudori, it was towed in this mode.
A space fighter that doubles as gear for the Gundam Mk-II. Alone it fights like a mobile suit; docked with the Mk-II, it boosts toughness, range and firepower.
Docked, its cockpit splits off as a small escape craft.
The Gundam Mk-II docked with the G-Defenser. It covers the Mk-II's weak armor and adds firepower with the G-Defenser's main gun, the Long Rifle.
The Mk-II can also dock with it in G-Defenser form, called the G-Flyer (not in this game). In Super Gundam form the G-Defenser's Core Fighter detaches, so unlike in this game,
it really seats one.
A prototype transforming mobile suit Anaheim built for the AEUG. A milestone of Anaheim's Project Zeta, its prototypes spawned the Hyaku Shiki, Methuss and more,
and its successors the Zeta Plus, ZZ Gundam and Re-GZ: a legend. It merges the Mk-II's movable frame, the Rick Dias's armor and Kamille's ideas (like the Mk-II's Flying
Armor). In Waverider form it can reenter with no ballute or other options, and can fly in atmosphere.
In MS form it's also highly mobile, and its high-output generator powers strong arms like the Hyper Mega Launcher. A later bio-sensor
greatly improves its response. Judau flew it early in Gundam ZZ, and kept using it when speed mattered even after the ZZ appeared.
The Zeta Gundam's high-speed mode. Transforming aims its verniers backward for huge mobility; its thrust even lets it fly in atmosphere.
Its biggest merit is reentry with no ballute or other options, which gives the Zeta Gundam great strategic value.
A variant with different Flying Armor, the "Wave Shooter," also seems to exist.
A mobile suit evolved from the Zeta Gundam, read "Zeta Two." Its simpler transformation is easier to build and fly, but it lost reentry ability.
Its transformation seems based on the Methuss. In fact the ZZ Gundam took priority, so the Zeta II plan was scrapped. Thus later Zeta-line mobile suits
(Zeta Plus, Re-GZ) didn't carry on its concept.
The Zeta II's mobile armor mode. It can't reenter, so it's used as a space fighter.
A prototype mobile suit built by Anaheim Electronics for the AEUG, designed by Dr. M. Nagano. Made as a transforming suit under Anaheim's Project Zeta,
it had a structural flaw, so transformation was dropped. Still, it performed well enough for combat and went to the Argama. Its hallmark is golden armor, which
reportedly also resists beams. The "hundred" in its name means "a suit to last 100 years." A generator able to power the optional Mega Bazooka Launcher alone,
high mobility from its flexible back binder, and Quattro's skill won it many victories, starting with the Jaburo assault. Wrecked in the final battle with Haman, but in Gundam ZZ unit 2
joined the Argama, mostly flown by Beecha.
An improved Hyaku Shiki. Likely built by Anaheim for the AEUG once Nemo and GM types couldn't match Titans suits, but there's no record of Quattro flying it.
A high-mobility device replaces its flexible back binder, boosting mobility further, and it carries more weapons. Other Hyaku Shiki types are the mass-produced Hyaku Shiki Kai,
ground type and Full Armor version.
An arms plan for the Hyaku Shiki Kai, adding beam and live-ammo weapons for firepower and chest reflector panels for defense. But as big transforming suits took over,
it was never mass-produced.
A prototype transforming mobile suit by Anaheim Electronics, built under Anaheim's Project Zeta. Its mobility was fine, but
its frame was fragile and its MS performance mediocre, so only one was deployed, to the Argama. Known for its pipe-like waist and fixed arm beam guns.
It appeared early in Gundam ZZ too, but seems to have left the field when Fa did.
MA mode of a prototype transforming suit by Anaheim Electronics, apparently a transformation test. Once done, it went to the Argama as a fast space fighter.
A general-purpose mobile suit built by Anaheim Electronics for the AEUG. Its armor is Gundarium alloy, made with Zeon tech, so it resembles a Dom.
Developed as the Gamma Gundam; Quattro had it named after navigator Bartholomew Dias. Only his unit was red, but after he took the Hyaku Shiki, all units
were repainted in his colors.
A general-purpose mobile suit built by Anaheim Electronics for the AEUG. Its armor is Gundarium alloy, made with Zeon tech, so it resembles a Dom.
Developed as the Gamma Gundam; Quattro had it named after navigator Bartholomew Dias. This was the standard color, but after Quattro took the Hyaku Shiki,
the craze for his red faded it out. Maybe two colors was a hassle...
MS mode of a Federation transforming mobile armor. It turns into a saucer-like lifting body to fly in atmosphere. In Zeta Gundam,
Bran Blutarch flew one, troubling Kamille's Mk-II on Earth and downing Roberto's Rick Dias. Later mass-produced for Dakar.
A Federation transforming mobile armor. Its thick armor is tough, but it's defenseless the instant its chest closes as it becomes a mobile suit.
The Titans' main cruiser. The Titans have several sister ships with small differences, like the Hario and Lombardia. One appears at the end of Gundam 0083, crewed by
ex-Albion bridge crew Pasarov and Simone. Maybe they died with Jamaican in the attack by Emma's Super Gundam...
Scirocco's own transforming suit, which becomes a fast mobile armor. Flown by his men Jerid and Mouar, its power, speed and teamwork overwhelmed Kamille's Mk-II.
It also has a middle form, legs spread to bare its MA claws.
The Gabthley's mobile armor mode. Rear-massed thrusters give high mobility, and its leg movable frames serve as claws for close combat.
Neo Zeon's prototype Newtype mobile suit, known for its huge shoulder armor. Code-named "Elmeth 2" as an MS version of the One Year War's Newtype mobile armor Elmeth.
It has Funnels, psycommu weapons that attack from all ranges, and shoulder binders that double as flexible thrusters for amazing mobility. And flown by Haman,
a strong Newtype, it truly became Neo Zeon's symbol. Haman's is prototype 1; improved units 2 and 3 (Qubeley Mk-II) and mass-produced models also exist.
A super-large battleship evolved from Zeon's Gwazine class. By Gwazine tradition, it carries Neo Zeon's elite, Mineva Zabi included. Weaker in firepower than the Titans'
Dogosse Giar, but better in cruising range and acceleration.
A transforming Newtype mobile suit by the Murasame Lab; as named, an evolved Psyco Gundam. With psycommu weapons like a wired Beam Sword and reflector bits,
it hits harder than the Psyco Gundam. In the original, Rosamie, Rosamia Badam, flew it, until Kamille destroyed its head.
Neo Zeon then got it, and Ple Two flew it.
MA mode of a Murasame Lab transforming Newtype suit. Like the Psyco Gundam it has Minovsky craft, but this mode never appeared since it wasn't used in atmosphere.
Wrecked at the Gate of Zedan, it went to Neo Zeon, and in the sequel Gundam ZZ, Ple Two sortied in this mode to attack the Argama.
A heavy mobile suit Scirocco built for himself, read "The O." Packed with experiments like a bio-sensor, it's far more mobile and agile than
its bulk suggests. Hidden arms in its front skirt serve as concealed melee weapons, leaving no blind spot at any range.
A giant transport in the helium fleet bound for Jupiter. Besides living blocks, it has factory blocks. Scirocco used it to return from Jupiter
and stayed in the Earth Sphere with it as his base. Sister ships seem to exist; one appears in Gundam ZZ's finale.
A new large Titans battleship built at Gryps. The Titans' flagship, its MS capacity and firepower far outclass earlier ships.
A Federation mobile suit that can fly in atmosphere without a subflight system. With swapped thrusters, it works in space too.
A Federation transforming mobile suit with a psycommu, used mainly to control the unit and tuned at Augusta's Newtype lab.
Gates Capa flew silver unit 1, Rosamia Badam the reddish unit 2, and Jerid the yellow unit 3 (though he seems to have ended up in unit 2).
The Bound Doc's mobile armor mode, with tough armor and mobility. Its MS legs serve as claws for close combat. The underside, where the MS upper body is exposed,
is likely its weak point.
A heavy mobile suit Scirocco built himself, with heavy anti-ship guns that cost agility when fully loaded. Reccoa, who left for Scirocco, flew it in a death match with Emma's Mk-II.
A Titans transforming mobile suit. Its simpler transformation than the Gabthley's makes it easier to build. Known for its five mono-eyes and sharp, angular design.
It has the Sea Serpent electric whip for group attacks up close. Yazan, Ramsus and Dangel flew them against the AEUG, and near the atmosphere knocked Quattro's Hyaku Shiki
into Earth's gravity. Its beam rifle is the Feyedarlin rifle, same as the Gabthley's.
The Hambrabi's mobile armor mode. A simple change, but more mobile, with its arms used as claws up close. Its shoulder mono-eyes are used in this mode.
A mass-produced mobile suit built by Anaheim Electronics for the Titans. A stronger generator lets it fire two or more beam weapons at once, which the Hizack couldn't.
MS mode of a transforming mobile armor Scirocco built. It can use a Beam Saber for close combat. In the original, it was the first transforming unit seen;
Kamille and Emma were amazed by it.
A transforming mobile armor Scirocco built aboard the Jupitris. Strong thrusters made to escape Jupiter's gravity give it superb mobility; many built-in guns give it firepower.
A prototype transforming heavy mobile suit Anaheim built for the AEUG, the next Project Zeta unit after the Zeta Gundam. Concept: "an RX-78 and G-Armor in one unit."
So it inherits the Zeta's transformation and the RX-78's Core Block and G-Parts systems, made of a Core Fighter, upper Core Top and lower Core Base.
Each part flies as a fighter; combined, it becomes the heavy fighter-bomber G-Fortress. Built for firepower, it has many strong beam weapons, like its forehead High Mega Cannon.
But it eats energy, so its operating time is short. It's the peak of the power-driven suits of around U.C. 0087. Flown by Judau Ashta, it's the Gundam Team's core.
The ZZ Gundam's heavy fighter-bomber form, made of the Core Top (A-Part plus Core Fighter) and Core Base (B-Part plus Core Fighter). Used mainly for long trips.
The ZZ Gundam was meant as RX-78 and G-Armor in one, but the G-Fortress lacks the G-Armor's versatility. Still, its firepower is, around U.C. 0087,
the strongest.
A Neo Zeon heavy mobile suit. Based on the Psyco Gundam Mk-II, it has Incoms, wired quasi-psycommu weapons anyone can use. Its many guns give it great firepower;
a few were built for Rakan's Space Wolf Team, loyal to Glemy. Rakan's unit has hidden forearm arms that standard units lack.
The ZZ Gundam with extra armor. It can't transform, but the armor boosts its defense and its already high firepower. To keep its mobility with the added armor,
the body got a stronger backpack and more ("Enhanced ZZ Gundam"). It also carries the Hyper Mega Cannon (unseen in the show), among the strongest MS handheld guns,
so it looks much like the FAZZ of Gundam Sentinel.
The Full Armor ZZ Gundam's heavy fighter-bomber form, used mainly for long trips. The real Full Armor ZZ Gundam can't turn into a G-Fortress.
A Neo Zeon melee mobile suit for knights (commanders), following the concept of Zeon's One Year War YMS-15 Gyan. Its signature weapon is
a beam rifle with a bayonet.
A Neo Zeon cruiser. Several sister ships differ in color, like the yellow Mindora and navy Sandora.
Successor to Neo Zeon's Gaza-C, with the same transformation and many shared parts, but more firepower. Early in the original, the Gaza Storm team's smoke-screen formation
troubled the green Judau.
The Gaza-D's mobile armor mode. In this form it can fly in atmosphere.
A Neo Zeon ground mobile suit for invading Earth. Built for melee, its signature weapon is the extending Arm Punch.
A Neo Zeon prototype Newtype mobile suit, improved from Haman's prototype 1. The black prototype 2 is flown by Ple. Its main change: its beam-gun
Beam Sabers are now three-pronged for a bit more power. Otherwise it equals prototype 1.
A Neo Zeon prototype Newtype mobile suit, improved from Haman's prototype 1. The red prototype 3 is flown by Ple Two. Unlike unit 2, it adds a
psycommu controller for remote use; else it equals units 1 and 2.
A Neo Zeon prototype Newtype mobile suit, improved from Haman's prototype 1. The black prototype 2 is flown by Ple. Its main change: its beam-gun
Beam Sabers are now three-pronged for a bit more power. Otherwise it equals prototype 1.
A giant Neo Zeon Newtype mobile suit. Besides Funnels, psycommu weapons, it has mega particle cannons and Beam Sabers for close combat.
Its head, also an escape pod, can fly alone. Glemy's trump card, flown by Ple Two, it wiped out the Gundam Team: Neo Zeon's strongest mobile suit.
A Neo Zeon Newtype mobile suit loaded with heavy guns, like its hyper mega particle cannon. Its child funnels, fired from mother funnels,
are two-stage, so they reach farther than other models'. Flown by Chara, loyal to Haman to the end, against Glemy's mass-produced Qubeleys.
A Neo Zeon prototype mobile suit, the last of the Zaku line. Highly versatile, swapping arms for each situation. But developed alongside the Doven Wolf,
it lost out in firepower and thrust, so only a few were built.
A custom Zaku III, based on its assault loadout, with more thrust and some new weapons. Mashymre, loyal to Haman, flew it against Glemy's side: Rakan's
Space Wolf Team.
A Neo Zeon rear-support mobile suit. Made to team with the melee-focused Galluss-J, it gives covering fire with missiles all over its body. With a booster that lets it fly in atmosphere,
it can also raid enemy lines, fire its missiles and pull out. And with the booster and Missile Pods removed, for close combat it has
a Beam Saber too.
Neo Zeon's final Dom-line mobile suit. Built for the Earth landing, but performs well in space too. Mostly melee gear, notably the Tri-Blade cutters.
A Neo Zeon transforming mobile suit. Its upper and lower halves split into the Bawoo Attacker and Bawoo Nutter, the Nutter radio-guided by the Attacker.
Glemy's prototype is all orange, with the kanji for "flying dragon" on its skirt. Mass-produced units are green.
A Neo Zeon prototype mobile suit, highly mobile thanks to thrusters all over. Its triple arm beam cannons are wired psycommu weapons capable of
all-range attacks. High-performance but picky about pilots, so it wasn't mass-produced. Mashymre flew it and wrecked Judau's Zeta Gundam.
A mass-produced Federation mobile suit Anaheim built from all its GM-series tech. Thrusters all over give it high mobility, and it carries varied weapons.
Londo Bell's mainstay, used until the U.C. 0120s.
A Newtype mobile suit of Char Aznable's Neo Zeon. Its built-in psycoframe gives response far beyond older models. Heavily armored, but thrusters all over
make it agile and mobile: a mighty unit fit for Neo Zeon's leader, Char. Besides Funnels, it has mega particle cannons and more for huge firepower.
A Newtype mobile suit Anaheim built with all its might at Londo Bell's request. Its pilot, Amuro, helped design it; the culmination of all Gundams,
a supreme machine. The new psycoframe material, given by Neo Zeon's leader Char Aznable, is used around the cockpit and drive, for superb response and agility.
The psycoframe also runs its hallmark fin funnels, the first psycommu weapons on a Gundam. Bigger and stronger than normal Funnels, they act as mega particle guns
and can combine to make a magnetic field for a beam barrier. It also carries a balanced mix of beam, live-ammo and melee weapons.
It fought a death match with Char's Sazabi on the falling Axis, then, to stop Axis falling, its psycoframe resonance formed a strange force field. Its arms, performance, and pilot
Amuro's skill make it arguably the strongest Gundam.
The Nu Gundam with the Full Armor concept found in past Gundam plans. It wears the Heavy Weapon System; to offset the weight of armor like its bigger shield,
extra boosters keep it mobile. It also carries a Hyper Mega Rifle for more firepower.
A Newtype mobile suit of Char Aznable's Neo Zeon. It reuses the Geara Doga's movable frame, but with a high-output generator.
Added apogee motors and more greatly boost mobility. It has varied arms plus Funnels, but it's a rush job, falling short as a Newtype unit.
Two saw combat. Gyunei's is blue, with long head antennas.
A Newtype mobile suit of Char Aznable's Neo Zeon. Of the two in combat, Quess's is reddish, with shorter head antennas than Gyunei's.
And while Gyunei's uses a beam assault rifle, hers uses a mega Gatling Gun.
Flagship of the Federation's Londo Bell. Besides normal launch catapults, it has a landing deck at the stern, and an armored combat bridge apart from its normal bridge.
The Jeanne d'Arc in Victory Gundam is its sister ship.
The Re-GZ's mobile armor mode with the Back Weapon System. Agility, cruising range and firepower all leap. But the Back Weapon System
is near-disposable; once shed to become a mobile suit, it can't be refitted (in the field).
A prototype mobile suit built by Anaheim for Londo Bell. A simplified, mass-producible Zeta Gundam that becomes a mobile armor with the Back Weapon System.
This keeps performance high while easing production. Still far pricier than other mass-produced units, so only one was deployed, to Londo Bell.
"Re-GZ" stands for "Refined Gundam Zeta."
A giant Newtype mobile armor of Char Aznable's Neo Zeon, the trump card of the plan to freeze Earth by dropping Axis. Where legs would be,
it has huge Sturm thrusters, making it quite mobile for its size. Quess Paraya flew it, plaguing Londo Bell with Funnels and massive firepower.
A mass-produced mobile suit of Char Aznable's Neo Zeon: the sum of Zeon tech, highly versatile with swappable gear for each role.
Easy to build, it's Neo Zeon's mainstay. By Zeon tradition, units of squad leaders and up have head horns.
Rezin's Geara Doga, custom-tuned as her own and repainted mainly blue.
Flagship of Char Aznable's Neo Zeon, evolved from Zeon's Gwazine class. A large ship with top-class MS capacity and firepower.
A Newtype mobile suit evolved from the Nu Gundam. Unlike the Nu Gundam, rushed into the Second Neo Zeon War, it was finished after full testing.
Besides a powerful hyper mega beam launcher, its backpack funnel pods recharge the fin funnels, so compared to the Nu Gundam
its attack power is even higher. From the novel "Char's Counterattack," which has several versions, it was seen as another name for the Nu Gundam, but lately it's officially
been made the Nu Gundam's successor.
A small high-performance mobile suit from the Formula Project of the Federation navy's strategy institute, SNRI. Read "Formula Ninety-One." Based on data from the earlier F90,
it uses new tech like a beam shield, a high-output generator and a bio-computer that syncs with the pilot's mind for power. Fixed arms like the Mega Machine Cannon
were also bolstered. When the Crossbone Vanguard hit Side 4, Seabook, who managed to link its unfinished bio-computer and became its pilot by chance, took it into battle.
At its limit, its parts open to vent heat, and paint peeled off by the heat leaves afterimage-like traces. These "afterimages with mass" fool enemy sensors and eyes.
A prototype commander's mobile suit by the Crossbone Vanguard. Its fin nozzles, evolved from the movable shelf nozzles of the Berga Dalas and others, give high mobility.
A mass-produced Crossbone Vanguard MS. Unlike the close-range Den'an Zon, it's a mobile all-rounder.
The first Den'an series unit, built for close combat. It has many new technologies, like a goggle-type camera eye, beam shield and Shot Lancer.
The Crossbone Vanguard's main MS.
A commander's suit by the Buch Concern, parent of the Crossbone Vanguard. Movable shelf nozzles give it unmatched mobility. Versus its sibling Berga Dalas, its sensors and
thrusters are improved.
An anti-personnel killing machine built under Carozzo Ronah (Iron Mask)'s "Rafflesia Project" to wipe out surplus population. Its sensors detect human breath and body heat
to attack, and it's no weaker than a mobile suit. It holds even smaller Bugs inside, called "Baby Bugs."
A commander's mobile suit built by the Buch Concern, parent of the Crossbone Vanguard. This color is Zabine's, leader of the elite Black Vanguard.
A commander's mobile suit built by the Buch Concern, parent of the Crossbone Vanguard, specced for close combat. A bit weaker than the Berga Giros,
but its arms are nearly the same.
A giant space mobile armor from the Rafflesia Project of Crossbone commander Carozzo. Shaped like five petals, armed for all directions and ranges.
It's controlled via cables linked to Carozzo's iron mask.
A highly adaptable Gundam that gives its best anywhere. "Spiegel" means mirror; as named, it's a ninja-like unit that blends into its surroundings. Spreading its Spiegel Blades,
it spins like a top to shred foes: its finisher, Sturm und Drang. The name is German for "storm and stress," originally a literary movement of Goethe and others.
An MF Neo Japan built for the Gundam Fight finals. It beats the Shining Gundam in every way; even Domon, master of the Shining Gundam, was overwhelmed by its power.
Its Bakunetsu God Finger is deadly.
Its back wings open like a halo. Its chest cover opens to reveal an energy crystal, and the King of Hearts crest appears.
A Mobile Fighter made by Dr. Mikamura for Neo Japan's Gundam Fight. Mobile Fighters are built to Gundam Fight regulations; their main difference from mobile suits:
the cockpit is the Mobile Trace System. This "revolutionary" system relays the pilot's moves directly, so a Mobile Fighter pilot must be a great martial artist
(or close to it) to bring out its power. The Shining Gundam has untold potential to unleash human power, with three modes: Normal, Battle and Super.
Its Shining Finger uses liquid metal; while in use, its joints glow to shed heat.
The Shining Gundam in Super Mode, triggered when Domon's emotions (mostly rage) peak. Its head cooling cover, leg covers and shoulder magnet field generators open
for forced cooling. There's also a true Super Mode, triggered by mastering Meikyo Shisui, whose power overwhelmed even Master Asia. Meikyo Shisui means
a heart like still, clear water.
In the original, Neo Sweden's Gundam, the only female-type in the 13th tournament. Built for speed and flexibility, its armor is cut to the bone; it toys with foes by its quick moves.
It attacks with a Beam Ribbon and Beam Hoop in gymnastics-like moves.
The Nobel Gundam in Berserker Mode: its hair-like cooling fins spread and its body turns reddish. Berserker Mode is triggered by remotely seizing the pilot's brainwaves;
using a subliminal system to manipulate "negative" feelings like anger and grief, it maxes the unit's potential, rivaling God Gundam's Hyper Mode in power.
As proof, the Nobel Gundam in Berserker mode crushed Bolt Gundam in seconds.
Leader of the Devil Gundam's Four Kings. Out of battle, it wears its wings like a cloak-shield. Its arms can stretch or fly out on beam wires. It also has
the "Darkness Finger," rival to the Shining Finger, and Master's beam cloth, which a Beam Saber can cut.
Master Gundam riding Fuunsaiki. It overcomes the Mobile Fighter's weakness: limited moves in midair.
The original's Four Kings combined. Major Ulube flew it at the Shuffle Alliance, but lost to their combo.
Born of the Devil Gundam's self-multiplication. Weak alone, but it moves in huge groups and swarms at once. Base of the Devil Gundam's Death series, with flying, aquatic
and other variants. Its weapon, a club-shaped beam rifle, works for melee and shooting.
A Death Army with a horse-like four-legged walker. Unlike the club of a normal Death Army, it carries a rifle-like weapon. Otherwise it's the same as a Death Army.
If the legs are destroyed, it keeps fighting as a normal Death Army.
A Death Army with a water unit, armed with a Trident. In the original it sometimes fired the add-on like a torpedo. Like other variants, without the add-on
it works as a normal Death Army.
A Death Army variant joined to a flight unit in a birdlike form. It has a big Beam Cannon, but like the rest, its best weapon is numbers. Without the flight unit,
it works as a normal Death Army.
A Death Army copy of Master Gundam: far weaker, but with its look and basic arms. In the original, Master Asia sent them at Domon.
The twisted form of the Ultimate Gundam, built by Domon's father Dr. Raizo Kasshu and brother Kyoji Kasshu. To revive Earth, the Ultimate Gundam was given three principles:
self-evolution, self-multiplication and self-regeneration. But when Kyoji took it to Earth, the shock of reentry broke it, and it ran wild as the Devil Gundam. With the three principles,
its Devil Gundam Cells (DG Cells) have terrible infesting power, spawning minions like the Death Army and Gundam Heads, giant tentacle heads; it's a strong fighter too.
In the original Domon wrecked it in Shinjuku, Guiana and Lantau Island, but it always regenerated.
The Devil Gundam's final form, with Rain, the ideal woman as bio-unit, inside. Ulube took its wreck from Lantau Island and made it the core of Neo Japan's colony, now Devil Colony.
An odd shape: an upper body like the Shining Gundam's, and a lower body formed from a giant head. It looks slow, but glides swiftly over the ground.
It fights with huge stretching arms from its shoulders and beams from all over. Rain, its bio-unit, powers it with her emotion of rejecting Domon.
Na's aura battleship, captained by Kawasse Goo. Unlike other aura battleships, it has a vertical build for 3D combat.
Rau's aura battleship. After King Foizon's death, his granddaughter Ele commands it with captain Abe Tamari. Its bow Aura Nova Cannon gives it great firepower.
It's also the largest of the four aura battleships.
An Aura Battler made by Ah: the final form of the Aura Battler, fast, heavily armed and armored, a match for the Billbine. Besides the Black Knight's black unit, Musie's
white one, pink ones for regular troops, and others exist.
A prototype Aura Battler built by Shot Weapon and Earthling engineer Zett Wright on Drake's orders. Thinner armor than the Drumlo of its time, but faster and more agile.
Its performance mirrors the pilot's aura very directly, so it's hard to handle, but with strong aura it can beat later units. First flown by Show, then handed to Marvel,
it fought from start to end of the original. Three were built, Show's included.
A recolor of Show's Dunbine, mainly dark blue, flown by Todd Guinness. After Marvel shot it down,
it was salvaged for spare parts for Show's. Besides Show's and Todd's, there was also a dark green one flown by Tokamak Lobsky.
A Ku Aura Battler: balanced and strong, later mass-produced as Drake's mainstay. Armed with a tomahawk Aura Sword, which it sometimes threw in the original.
Ku's Red Three Knights used red-painted units, and with the Tripler, a three-unit chain attack, troubled Show's Billbine.
Na's newest transforming Aura Battler. It can become a Wing Caliber, reaching and leaving the battlefield faster than any before. Highly mobile and agile, with the Aura Cannon
and Aura Sword Rifle, rapid-fire guns that make it good at mid range. It also has a new weapon, the Aura Beam Sword. But mastering it
takes strong aura, so it went to Show, whom Na's Queen Sheela Lapana saw as a true Holy Warrior.
The transforming Aura Battler Billbine's high-speed cruise form. "Wing Caliber" refers to aura machines for fast transport and support of Aura Battlers.
It can't melee, the Aura Battler's main style, but suits long, fast travel; in the original it often ferried other Aura Battlers to the front.
The Billbine with night camo for the final battle with Drake's army. In the original it performs no differently from the normal colors.
The Billbine's cruise form with night camo for the final battle with Drake's army. In the original it performs no differently from the normal colors.
A prototype Aura Battler of Drake's army. Earthling engineer Zett Wright did the main work, but Shot's scheming lets it draw a commoner's aura to the limit.
So as Garalia Nyamhee's own unit, it drew out her aura fully, and its fight with Show's Dunbine opened the Aura Road. Later, a few
were mass-built by Zett and Shot.
A mass-produced Aura Battler co-developed by Rau and Na. An evolved Bozune, strong in air combat, and the anti-Drake mainstay. Production units are green, but
Marvel's was reddish, and King Foizon of Rau's own unit dark blue.
An Aura Battler of Drake's army, one of the last developed. Well-balanced for near and far. In the original it went Hyper from Todd's aura.
Flagship aura battleship of Drake's army. Flying by pseudo-aura generators, it also carries Aura Battlers and aura ships.
An aura fighter with the strengths of an Aura Battler and a Wing Caliber. Rather than melee, it excels at fast hit-and-run.
Flagship aura battleship of Bishot's army. Mostly hangar inside, it carries more Aura Battlers than any other, but has weaker attack and defense.
Shot's personal aura cruiser. Weaker in firepower than aura battleships, but as fast as a Wing Caliber. With his own ship,
Shot acted apart from Drake to pursue his own ambitions.
An Aura Battler Shot built on Drake's orders. Thicker armor than the Dunbine of its time, with built-in guns. Stable and easy to use, it was mass-produced as Drake's
mainstay until late in the war. Usually red, though Todd had a dark blue one.
Jeryl's Leprechaun gone Hyper. Going Hyper is when runaway aura makes the aura barrier take the Aura Battler's shape and grow huge,
greatly boosting attack power too.
The aura fighter Garaba gone Hyper from a malicious aura. Its attacks are unchanged, but its huge size and runaway aura wreak destruction.
An aura bomber by Shot, more mobile and powerful than Aura Battlers, with Wire Claws for melee. Musie flew it against Show and co.
An Aura Battler Shot built: a new design with guns built in all over, but poorly balanced, weak in armor and such. Flown by Jeryl Kuchibi,
it was the first to go Hyper.
A combat super robot: a prototype Megaborg built by Sozo Haran on Mars, stolen and modified by his son Banjo. It has a solar-powered pulse ion engine and special steel Da armor.
It transforms into the heavy fighter Daifighter and heavy tank Daitank. It holds the small transforming fighter Mach Attacker, whose cockpit moves inside to become Daitarn 3's.
It's apparently very easy to pilot; in the original, Garrison, Beauty, Reika and even Toppo flew it. Hugely agile despite its size, it moves as nimbly as a human in the original.
Even its face changes, though it's unclear if it has a will. The Daitarn Fan is for defense and offense; once it even frantically fanned back an enemy's poison powder,
among other uses.
Daitarn 3's heavy tank form, for terrain or underground where Daitarn 3 struggles. A simple change; its sliding treads retract and store on its back
in Daitarn 3 form.
Daitarn 3's heavy fighter form, mainly for long trips. When Banjo raises his pendant and shouts "Daitarn, come here!", it comes from beyond the horizon, wherever he is.
It's also the base form for holding the Mach Attacker.
From episode 32 of the original: toys in the collection of toy-loving commander Torres. Identical to Daitarn 3, but only half its size.
A simplified mass-produced Daifighter (Daitarn 3's heavy fighter form). Same as the original minus transformation. Seen in the final Meganoid battle, but in other colors.
A small Meganoid fighter.
Don Zauser grown giant: unlike a Megaborg, he grows in human form. In the original he grows when Koros is in danger, and loses to Banjo on Mars.
In the original, a chimera made in Dr. Animad's bio-synthesis experiments. It seemed to have free will, but Dr. Animad, seeking to catch Banjo, fitted a cockpit unit to pilot it.
Already huge, it became a Megaborg to face Daitarn 3, bigger and fiercer. It has Megaborg arms, like eye Ring Beams, mouth Flamethrower and finger Missiles, and beastly Bites.
It finally falls to the Sun Attack.
The ultimate tank built by Commander Hessler, far bigger than the Daitank. In the original, Megaborg Hessler had the upper hand, but shielding the Nibelgen from destruction,
Defeated by Daitarn 3. After Hesler died, Banjo, fearing it would fall back into Meganoid hands, rebuilt it as a radio-controlled toy for Toppo.
Koros enlarged by micromachines.
Commander Mylene as a Meganoid. Fights with her sword and a belt flamethrower, and snares foes with her lion-like mane. In the original, mind waves from her sword
even briefly enslaved Daitarn 3 (and its pilots, Banjo and the rest).
In ep. 7, Commander Duston tried to warp a city to Mars with a Teleport Machine. This Meganoid robot was built from his Megaborg data. In ep. 13, Megaborg Benmel and Neros
were also reused as battle robots.
Neros as a Megaborg. Deft with its Blue Dragon Blade, it even broke the Daitarn Javelin. It also had eye rays, mouth flames, shoulder mines and missiles, and arm cutters,
making it quite the all-rounder.
Commander Benmel's giant form, with a crude, rugged look. Despite that, it deftly wielded a polearm with sickles at both ends, and fired missiles from pipes on its shoulders.
A Meganoid robot from episode 9. Its main weapon is, naturally, its leg drill, used to ram foes or fired off at them.
A samurai-like combining robot the Bialians brought to Earth after the Gaizok destroyed planet Bial. It combines three machines: Zanbird, Zambull and Zambase.
Zanbird can become a robot, Zambo Ace. Dug up by the Jin family when the Gaizok invaded, it is flown by sleep-trained kids Kappei, Uchuta and Keiko. Arms include the Arm Punch,
the Zambot Buster (knee discs thrown at foes), the Buster Missile it fires, and the hip-fired Bull Missile, plus the Zambot Grap, Cutter and Blow, which take three forms (sai, sword, spear)
as melee weapons. Its finisher: the Zambot Moon Attack, fired from its brow crescent. It can also use King Bial's Ion Cannon.
A Gaizok guardian god, twin of Red Knight Deathcain save for its color and right-hand lance. It fires beams from lance and shield; the shield is very sturdy.
With Deathcain, it also used a combo attack: both flash their shields, then hurl weapons at the dazzled foe.
A Gaizok guardian god, with Blue Knight Helldain. Its humanoid torso rides a horse-headed chariot. It fights with sword and shield, firing beams from the shield.
With Helldain, it may flash its shield brightly to blind the enemy.
A Mecha Boost sent after King Bial. Its icy breath can freeze a big transport whole. Its body is a cluster of mini H-bombs; when destroyed, it splits into bombs
that cling magnetically. In the original, reverse magnetism pried them off; then timers blew them up.
The Gaizok god itself. But what...?
A bizarre-looking Mecha Boost that attacked Tokyo with mouth flames and missiles from who knows where. In the original, its body had an energy-reflecting metal coat,
shrugging off even the Moon Attack.
Gaizok mobile fortress and base, like a giant clay centaur. Armed with the Bandock Cannon and one-eyed homing Bandock Missiles, it has a strong barrier;
in the original, the Bial II was lost ramming its generator.
Bandock's head, detached. Just the head dwarfs Zambot. In the original, Butcher boards it on Gaizok's orders and, with Red Knight Deathcain and Blue Knight Helldain,
challenges them to a final battle.
A bird-man Mecha Boost with a second face on its belly; fights with mouth flames and a stretchy neck. It pressed Zambo Ace, but fell to Zambot 3's first Zambot Cutter.
A Mecha Boost for the final battle with King Bial and Zambot 3. Its Elementary Particle Laser rivals the Moon Attack. It also uses a Flamethrower and head Bazooka,
and its tail weight detaches to fire a snaring wire. In the original it pressed Zambot hard, but the Zambot Cutter cut it in two.
A Mecha Boost built from Bandock's tanks, with twin double-barreled turret heads. Heavily armored, it has head cannons, a big left-arm drill and a right-arm anchor wire.
Female-type robot by the Photon Power Laboratory's Prof. Yumi. Built to mine Japanium, it was armed against Dr. Hell. Later, a Demonic Mechanical Beast wrecked it,
and it gave up its place as Mazinger Z's partner to Dianan A.
Replacing the destroyed Aphrodite A as Mazinger Z's female partner. A bike, the Scarlet Mobile, docks to its head as cockpit. Unlike Aphrodite A, it was made from the start
to fight Mechanical Beasts, so it is stronger, but a cockpit that is just the Scarlet Mobile (a bike) is arguably more dangerous than Boss Borot.
A robot Boss forced the Photon Power Laboratory's three professors to build. Though made of scrap, it sometimes managed to help Mazinger Z and Great Mazinger.
Boss also had it upgraded in all sorts of ways as needed.
A super robot Dr. Juzo Kabuto spent 15 years building. But Baron Ashura's Iron Mask agents killed him, and Mazinger Z passed to his grandson Koji.
It runs on Photon Power energy, with armor of Super Alloy Z refined from Japanium ore. Armed head to toe, its combat power is said to rival the US Seventh Fleet.
It could not fly alone at first, but later overcame that by docking with the crimson wings, the Jet Scrander. The Jet Scrander has variable wings that, for flight beyond Mach 2.3,
sweep back. Like Mazinger, the Scrander is made of Super Alloy Z, and it has built-in weapons such as the Southern Cross Knife. Mazinger is also fitted with a kind of
overboost system, Mazin Power, which Koji used when in a pinch.
Dr. Hell's Mechanical Beast, from ep. 8, "Great Demon God Abdora Unmasked!!" Hiding in a park's giant statue, it wrecked the city at night.
A Mechanical Beast built by Dr. Hell. Appears with Doublas M2 in eps. 1, "Wonder Robot Born," and 2, "Stop the Ashura Corps." The first Mechanical Beast Mazinger Z fought.
The first Demonic Mechanical Beast, lent to Dr. Hell by Mykene vanguard Duke Gorgon. Ep. 69, "Hover Pilder Melts in Midair!" Its soft body outdid all prior Beasts.
It spits a dissolving fluid, which it used to destroy the Hover Pilder.
Dr. Hell's aquatic Mechanical Beast, from ep. 18, "Glossum, Pirate Gangster of the Sea!" Its head pincers and torpedoes sank ships, and it once beat Mazinger Z underwater.
But this led rocketry expert Dr. Gordon and his daughter Rita to fit Mazinger Z with underwater jets, improving its underwater ability.
Dr. Hell's flying Mechanical Beast. From ep. 34, "Crimson Lightning: Flying Mazinger." Loaded with 10,000 t of explosives, it even blew its hand up on the Laboratory barrier,
putting Koji in mortal danger. But it was easily beaten by Mazinger Z, now fitted with the Jet Scrander.
Dr. Hell's Mechanical Beast modeled on Baron Ashura, who fell to Mazinger Z. Used to avenge him in ep. 79, "One Second Before Mazinger Explodes!!"
A Mechanical Beast built by Dr. Hell. From episode 66, "Genova M9, the Unseen Assassin." A long-range sniper, it tormented Mazinger Z by attacking from beyond radar range.
Very proud and utterly sure of its skill, it took its own life on realizing it had lost.
A Mechanical Beast based on giants Dr. Hell found on Bardos Island. In eps. 1, "Wonder Robot Born," and 2, "Stop the Ashura Corps."
Dr. Hell's Mechanical Beast. Appears in the movie "Mazinger Z vs. Devilman." Notable for its four legs and huge horn, it excels, as you'd guess, at
ramming foes with that horn.
A Mechanical Beast built by Dr. Hell. From episode 91, "Last Chance!! Dr. Hell's Deadly Battle!!" It guards his lair, Hell Island, firing harpoons from its arms and legs to drag
Mazinger Z into the sea.
Brocken's flying fortress. Launches Mechanical Beasts from its mouth; has an inner factory. Runs a month unsupplied, hidden in cloud-smoke. Also carries his Iron Cross Corps'
paratroopers.
Baron Ashura's new undersea fortress after Mazinger Z sank Saluud. Mechanical Beasts launch from the mouth of the face atop its hull. It also carries subs, jet fighters,
paratroopers and more.
A combat super robot Dr. Kenzo Kabuto based on Mazinger Z, foreseeing the Mykene invasion. It runs on Photon Power energy, with Super Alloy New Z armor.
It is piloted from the small fighter Brain Condor, which docks into Great Mazinger ("Fire On"). And the retractable wings in its back, the Scramble Dash, let it reach Mach 4
in flight. Most of its weapons share Mazinger Z's concepts, but it has distinctive ones: the Mazinger Blade, strong in close combat, and the ultra-high-voltage Thunder Break.
The later Great Booster boosted its mobility and firepower (though it ended up disposable). Its weak point is the Scramble Dash housing; a hit there briefly
paralyzes all of its functions.
Dr. Kenzo Kabuto's female-type combat robot, Great Mazinger's partner against the coming Mykene. Piloted from the fighter Queen Star. Combat-built from the start,
it is strong enough to face Battle Beasts. The later Venus Scrander lets it fly.
A mass-produced Great Mazinger from Gosaku Ota's manga "Great Mazinger." Shinsumi Heavy Industries, maker of the GMFA1, stole Great Mazinger's plans to build it.
Its looks and performance are basically the original's, but the mass-produced units have numbers on their chests. In the story, to tell the original from the copies, Boss painted
"The Original" on the waist of Tetsuya's Great Mazinger. There is also one all-black mass-produced Great Mazinger.
A general from Mykene's enemy, reborn as a humanoid Battle Beast after losing to the Emperor of Darkness. Then his loyal servant, he led the seven Battle Beast legions
in the conquest of the surface. A valiant warrior, he finally fell in a duel with Great Mazinger. The sight of his men mourning his death
showed his stature as a true general, deeply trusted by his troops.
Appears in the Mazinger movie "Great Mazinger vs. Getter Robo." A space monster sent by a mysterious saucer to invade Earth. Hatched from an egg, it ate iron and other metals
to store energy and grow, plaguing Great Mazinger and Getter Robo. From a bug-legged lizard to a second form with a humanoid torso, it absorbed the saucer's energy
and reached this humanoid final form. Always hard-armored, its final form's weak spot is the hole left by removing its waist sickle.
An evolved Gilgilgan. It fuses eaten metal at the cellular level, its whole body turning metal so it can use 100% of its stored energy. In this form, its defense and attack
rise dramatically. The hole in its waist from the third form is sealed too, leaving no real weak point. Note that Mecha Gilgilgan does not appear in the Mazinger movies;
it's a Super Robot Wars original.
A superhuman Battle Beast of the Mykene Empire. Appears in the movie "Mazinger Z vs. the Great General of Darkness" with other Battle Beasts of the Mykene vanguard.
Its spear drives Mazinger Z to the brink of destruction. It is also the foe Mazinger Z fought with Great Mazinger's borrowed Mazinger Blade.
A bird-type Mykene Battle Beast. In ep. 1, "Great Mazinger, Hero of the Skies," it pressed Tetsuya, not yet fighting at his best.
A reptile-type Mykene Battle Beast. In the Mazinger movies, it joins the Mykene vanguard to attack Tokyo and fight Mazinger Z.
A ghost-type Mykene Battle Beast from ep. 3, "Fiery Guts!! Wild Venus!!", Venus A's debut. Its body and head can split to act apart; the game uses the head alone.
From the movie "Grendizer, Getter Robo G, Great Mazinger: Showdown! The Great Sea Beast." The ancient sea creature Dragonosaurus, mutated by absorbing heavy oil.
Its eight necks regrow instantly when cut, and its huge body's raw power battered a super robot army led by Great Mazinger and Getter Robo G. Its soft body
absorbs the shock of solid rounds. The oil it absorbed is stored inside, so fire attacks there are its weakness. The one who noticed, after being swallowed by it, was
none other than Boss.
A ghost-type Mykene Battle Beast. In "Mazinger Z vs. the Great General of Darkness," it joins the Mykene vanguard, nearly destroying the Photon Power Laboratory.
It speaks articulately, showing Battle Beasts are mutated survivors of the ancient Mykene. On first seeing Dante, Koji Kabuto mistook it for a talking Mechanical Beast.
From the movie "Great Mazinger vs. Getter Robo G: Great Clash in the Sky." An invasion robot sent by mysterious aliens to fight both robots. Its glowing look
earned it the name Light-Wave Beast. It looks alive, but a mechanical body lies under its glowing skin. The glow is a strong barrier that repels physical blows, absorbs beams,
tormenting both robots. "Great Clash in the Sky" also sees Getter Robo G and Great Mazinger's Great Booster completed.
The Mykene Empire's flying fortress. Able to fight on land, sea and in the air, it carries the seven legions' generals and Battle Beasts to the front. Its four faces hold weapons.
Daisuke Umon's giant robot; he is Duke Fleed, prince of Fleed. Its origin is disputed: Fleed's guardian god, or built by Fleed scientists under King Vega's threats.
Its weapons: the Screw Crusher Punch, a bladed, spinning forearm launched at foes; the Hand Beam; the Antigravity Storm, a zero-g chest wave; the horn-fired Space Thunder;
and the Double Harken, formed from its two Shoulder Boomerangs, a varied and potent arsenal. Its strong security attacks anyone not of Fleed's royal line who tries to board.
Grendizer's flying saucer unit alone, or Grendizer docked with it as Spazer. True to "UFO Robo," it can even fly between stars alone. All weapons but the Antigravity Storm work,
and the Spazer has ruthless arms too: Spin Saucer discs, the Spin Drill fired from them, and the Melt Shower, a dissolving spray.
The first Saucer Beast the Vega Star Federation sent against Earth. It unfolds from a flat saucer like a turtle. Its attacks are basic: eye rays, mouth flames and saucer-form rams.
In the original, it fell to Grendizer's overwhelming arms in its debut.
Strongest Vega Beast, flown by Lady Gandal, Commander Gandal's other self in the original. Armed with claws and flames, it was beheaded by a charging Grendizer.
Saucer Beast of Commander Zigra of King Vega's guard. In the original, its saucer form, armored in Super Alloy Veganium, repelled all Grendizer's attacks; it rams with blades out.
It turned humanoid, pressing Grendizer with a Veganium shield.
As the name says, the flagship of King Vega, ruler of the Vega Star Federation. He moved it to the Skull Moon base when planet Vega exploded. A vast spaceship,
it fell to Duke Fleed at the end.
In the original, the first Vega Beast to hit Earth. Vega Beasts are giant cyborg beasts, stronger than Saucer Beasts. Strong enough to rip off Grendizer's arm,
it boasts a hide that repels Grendizer's every attack.
Sent by Commander Gandal in the original to back up Kirika, this Vega Beast fights with sword arms and Freeze Rays from eye and chest.
A Vega Star Federation carrier, holding many Minifos.
The Vega Star Federation's mass-produced attack saucer, flying with Beasts and carriers or scouting alone. Countless were downed.
A combining super robot of three fighters built by Dr. Saotome. Meant for space development, it was armed against Emperor Gore's Dinosaur Empire. It runs on Getter Rays,
with Getter Alloy armor. Getter-1 joins the Eagle, Jaguar and Bear from the head down. Its Getter Wings let it fly at Mach 2; it is mainly for air combat.
The strongest overall of Getter Robo's three forms, and the most used. The Missile Machine Gun Getter-1 uses in the game is from Ken Ishikawa's manga.
A combining super robot of three fighters built by Dr. Saotome. Meant for space development, it was armed against Emperor Gore's Dinosaur Empire. It runs on Getter Rays,
Its armor is Getter Alloy. Getter-2 joins the Jaguar, Bear and Eagle from the head down, for ground and underground combat. Besides its Drill Arm, its greatest weapon is
its speed: it runs at Mach 3 on land and dazzles foes with Getter Vision afterimages. Its Drill Arm also lets it burrow underground.
A combining super robot of three fighters built by Dr. Saotome. Meant for space development, it was armed against Emperor Gore's Dinosaur Empire. It runs on Getter Rays,
Its armor is Getter Alloy. Getter-3 joins the Bear, Eagle and Jaguar from the head down. Unlike the other two, it has treads for legs, and is mainly for underwater combat.
The strongest of the three forms, it also uses pilot Musashi's judo throw, the Daisetsuzan Oroshi.
A super robot by America's Dr. King, from ep. 21, "The Robot from America." Piloted by his son Jack, with sister Mary in the Hat Machine, a support mech and weapon.
The Hat Machine and its main gun transform freely; the gun becomes a sword or rifle as needed. It saved Getter from a Mechasaur attack, showing its great power.
A land Mechasaur of the Dinosaur Empire, from ep. 2, "Showdown! Three Great Mechasaurs." One of the three with Zu of the sea and Bado of the sky. Excels at horn charges.
A land Mechasaur from ep. 1, "Invincible! Getter Robo Go!" Its armor blocks even the Getter Beam.
A sea Mechasaur in ep. 2, "Showdown! Three Great Mechasaurs." One of the three with Zai and Bado; has a flesh and a mecha neck.
A land Mechasaur from ep. 18, "The Dinosaur Empire's Tough Guy." The second Mechasaur Zen, after the first lost to Getter-1, with better stats.
Dinosaur Empire battleship from eps. 50, "Emperor Gore's Last Strike," and 51, "The Empire's Last Day." Carrying 4 Mechasaurs and 200 bombers, this trump card
was sent out as a last gamble. Its armor and firepower befit the name "Invincible Battleship"; Getter Robo failed to strike its one weak spot, the inside, and was crippled.
Blaming himself, Musashi loaded bombs on the Command Machine Michiru usually flew and charged in, ready to die... and never came back.
A sky Mechasaur from ep. 2, "Showdown! Three Great Mechasaurs." With Zai of the land and Zu of the sea, one of the three.
A giant flying carrier Mechasaur, from ep. 41, "The Unseen Dinosaur Air Raid Squad." Hidden in thunderclouds, it launched Dinosaur Jets off its back to bomb all Japan.
A sky Mechasaur of the Dinosaur Empire, from ep. 42, "Set Course for the North Pole!" It launches Dinosaur Jets from its wings. General Bat flew it against the helpless,
meteor-hauling Getter Robo.
A fighter flown by dinosaur soldiers. The Get Machines handle them easily, but they fly in formation in great numbers. Some are led by Mechasaurs, others launch from inside
a Mechasaur's body.
A new Getter Robo built for combat by Dr. Saotome. Getter Ray amplifiers give it 10 times the first Getter's power, and its armor is the new Synthetic Steel G.
It fought Emperor Burai's Hyakki Empire. Getter Dragon joins Dragon, Liger and Poseidon, for air combat, piloted by Ryoma. Like Getter-1, it is the strongest form,
and its top finisher is the Shine Spark, added midway through "Getter Robo G." The game's Getter Laser Cannon is from Ken Ishikawa's manga.
Dr. Saotome's Getter Dragon for Getter Ray tests, stolen and mass-produced by Count Brocken. It cannot split or combine, but otherwise
it matches the original Getter Dragon. This is a game-original setting; it does not split into Get Machines and become a giant dragon.
A new Getter Robo built for combat by Dr. Saotome. Getter Ray amplifiers give it 10 times the first Getter's power, and its armor is the new Synthetic Steel G.
Getter Liger joins the Liger, Poseidon and Dragon, mainly for ground and underground combat, with Hayato piloting as on Getter-2. Like Getter-2, it is the fastest form,
using the Mach Special afterimage. Its right hand is a five-fingered manipulator that becomes a drill as needed. In the original, Getter Liger could fly from the start.
A new Getter Robo built for combat by Dr. Saotome. Getter Ray amplifiers give it 10 times the first Getter's power, and its armor is the new Synthetic Steel G.
Getter Poseidon joins the Poseidon, Dragon and Liger. Unlike Getter-3, it walks on two legs, and is mainly for underwater combat. Below the knee, its legs can fold into
treads. Its pilot is Benkei, who joined the Getter Team in place of Musashi, killed fighting the Dinosaur Empire. Unlike in the game, in the original it
never uses the Daisetsuzan Oroshi. Like Getter-3, it has the most power of the three. Later in "Getter Robo G," it was modified to fly.
The Hyakki Empire's combined trump card, fusing Mecha Juppoki, Raijuki, Anchuki, Kokakuki and Rinmaki. In the original, its bulk, beams and flames ravaged Japan's land and sea.
In the original, a Hyakki robot built by Hyakki scientist Tekkoki to surpass Getter Robo. Save for its ogre head, it resembles Getter Dragon. True to Tekkoki's goal,
it overwhelmed the Getter Team in every fight. It has a tomahawk like Getter Dragon's, a horn beam equal to the Getter Beam, and arms that transform, like Getter Liger's,
to fire missiles, among other weapons. It also matched or beat Getter Liger's speed, and though they never clashed, it likely had power at least equal to Getter Poseidon's.
Horned-skull Hyakki robot with Gatling Gun arms. In the original, kind old Hakkotsuki flew it, pressing the Getter Team with veteran skill.
A thunder-god Hyakki robot with fitting weapons: lightning swords, thrown bolts, discharges. In the original, it rampaged to hide work on the Combined Hyakki Robot,
and fell to the Shine Spark.
The ultimate Getter, made to unleash the Getter Rays' power and fight all threats to them and humanity. Shin Getter-1 joins Shin Eagle, Jaguar and Bear in order,
and is mainly for air combat. It can stop, start and turn as if ignoring inertia. But it needs vast Getter Rays to start, so even the Dragon had to be
used as an amplifier. The strongest of the three forms, it is piloted by Ryoma, as Getter Dragon was. At times it moves as if it had a will, and much about it is a mystery.
At full power, Shin Getter morphs into other forms, but normally it changes by splitting and rejoining its Get Machines. The Getter Blast Cannon is from Ken Ishikawa's manga.
The Shin Shine Spark is game-original, but the manga shows similar moves a few times.
The ultimate Getter, made to unleash the Getter Rays' power and fight all threats to them and humanity. Upper body Shin Jaguar, lower Shin Eagle, back Shin Bear:
this is Shin Getter-2, mainly for ground and underground combat. Faster than Getter Liger, it dazzles foes with afterimages via the Shin Mach Special.
The ultimate Getter, made to unleash the Getter Rays' power and fight all threats to them and humanity. It joins Shin Bear (upper), Jaguar (torso), Eagle (treads),
and is mainly for ground and underwater combat. Benkei pilots it, as he did Getter Poseidon.
A combining super robot Dr. Nanbara built with super-electromagnetic physics, foreseeing an alien invasion. Five machines, Battle Jet, Crusher, Tank, Marine and Craft:
these Battle Machines combine into it. Its cue: "Let's Combine!" Power: super-electromagnetic energy. Armor: Cermet. Combining needs all five pilots' brain waves
must be in sync, which only works once the small robot Ropet confirms it. It has many weapons, more being added in the original until there were nearly 20
(some not in the game). It may be the robot whose height and weight most Japanese know by heart.
Campbell's invasion commander: a giant stone statue that is really a computer holding a mind. It led Garuda, android of scientist Oleana, to think it was his mother
and swear total loyalty. It split Combattler V apart with the Narumagne Beam when it stormed the base, but Garuda, learning he had been lied to, struck it with Big Garuda.
Campbellian aerial fortress with eyeballs on seven radiating bridges. Able to teleport, it attacks and withdraws swiftly.
Janera's fortress airship for the final battle with Combattler V. Three heads spew Flame, Freeze Rays and Electric Shock; it fires dome spikes and whips up tornadoes.
Its armor repelled even the Super Electromagnetic Spin, but fell to a second on the same spot.
A giant battle robot built by Oleana, Campbell's commander for the invasion of Earth. Its design has much in common with the android Garuda.
Janera's pets Shishiris Kiba and Garo, merged and enlarged. It roams the skies, pressing Combattler with fangs, claws and flames. In the original, standing in for a hurt Hyoma,
Chizuru beat it with the Spin.
A battle cyborg of Campbell's invasion force. From ep. 1.
A battle cyborg of Campbell's invasion force, from ep. 25, "Tragedy of Grand General Garuda." Mia piloted this centaur at the risk of her life to get Garuda reinstated.
A dragonlike Magma Beast Warukimedes rode to clear his name. In the original, it raided the Nanbara Connection with Combattler in Paris. It fires Claw Missiles from its limbs
and charges as the Darklon Drill.
Dangel's final-battle Magma Beast; in the original, the illusionist Great I took this form after exploding. It turns to magma to confuse foes, and attacks even as magma.
With the Magma Dryer, Magma Storm and more, it was every bit Combattler's equal.
Mutropolis's all-purpose fighter, used for scouting, surveys and rescues, not just battle. In the original it seats three, and its cockpit top is the Spit Fighter, also an escape craft.
Mystic super robot of the ancient Mu Empire, 12,000 years old. Kept inert and golden in the God Mask Rock, it moves once Akira enters ("Fade In"). Powered by Mutron energy,
its Mutron metal armor repairs itself in the inert state. Much inside it is unexplained; late in the original, the Star of La Mu, a Mutron energy release device,
unleashed its true power. Its main finisher is God Bird, charging in bird form at Mach 7. In the original, it also took God Bird form to travel long distances.
Only Akira, heir to Mu Emperor La Mu, can pilot Raideen, which moves as one with his body.
The first Fossil Beast Raideen fought, made by the Demon Empire. From ep. 2, "Fossil Giant Beast Bastodon." Its huge arm blades stand out; it also appears in the opening.
But Akira, still new to Raideen, couldn't use God Bird yet, so it was beaten with the God Gorgon.
Kyoretsu Beasts Gander and Geldon, made by Gorai and Gekido Kyoretsu, merged by Barao: the first combined Kyoretsu Beast. With a huge hammer, dish cutters, flames and more,
it has the power of two beasts.
The Demon Empire's flying fortress, aka the Great Demon Dragon. A giant hand of rock, it has a face on each fingertip, all different. It also carries Dorome, and at times Fossil Beasts.
A Kyoretsu Kyoretsu Beast sent to seize the Star of La Mu from Akira's mother. With two necks and buzz-saw forelegs, it stalls Raideen with saws and heat rays. Its rear neck cut off,
Gekido's airship docked there. It broke Raideen's right leg and God Block, but the Gorgon Sword cut it down, Gekido and all.
Gorai Kyoretsu as a Kyoretsu Beast. It hits Raideen and Mutropolis with belly Banger Missiles, toe drills and Snake Caterpillars. In the original, even God Voice could not breach
its guard. But Princess Lemuria told Akira, "Demons' eyes never turn Kyoretsu Beast"; struck there, it reeled, and God Bird finished it.
A magic archer, as its name says, whose arrows torment Raideen. An odd Kyoretsu Beast that hid its heart in a kidnapped schoolgirl.
A Fossil Beast like Raideen. It spits arrows, and threw its right-hand part, also a sword, like a God Boomerang. It whistles when it spits arrows.
Small battle creatures of the Demon Empire with soft, jellyfishlike skin, acting on their own will. Led by Gante in large numbers, they mostly form the Fossil Beasts' vanguard.
Normally so huge it towers over Demon Island, its lower body rooted there. In the original, Raideen had to grow giant with the Star of La Mu and Mutron to fight it as an equal.
Prince Sharkin, made giant by Barao's power. In ep. 27, "Sharkin's Demonic Battle," he duels Akira's Raideen to the death.
A Demon Empire warship rebuilt from a Gante, tougher than before.
The Demons' guardian god, born from Barao's claws and hair harder than steel: a four-armed knight's torso on a dragon. On its upper arms, the Kyoretsu brothers'
vengeful faces. It shoots eye beams, breathes fire, and its mane stretches into a forked spear. Its blood seems to be magma; hit in the mouth by an Energy Cutter, it spewed magma,
and badly hurt, it still harmed Raideen. When Jinguji rammed it in the missile-laden Bluegar, it reeled, and God Bird cut it apart.
A custom Gespenst from Project ATX, a PT upgrade plan, based on the unnumbered test Unit 3. Model PTX-003C. "A machine whose sheer firepower breaks through head-on":
under that concept, almost all its arms are close/mid-range solid weapons, like the huge "Revolver Stake" pile driver and the titanium-ball "Square Claymore,"
shining in close combat. But its extreme, anachronistic concept and pilot-dependent controls ended development at one prototype, and the German "old iron" (Alteisen)
stuck as its shameful code name.
A custom Alteisen. Model PTX-003-SP1 (unofficial, a wartime special case). Using Weissritter spare parts, it mounts a weapon shelved for ruining the frame's balance:
the large-bore Revolver Bunker. Every weapon was upsized too. Its miraculous balance gives it explosive charging power.
"Riese" is German for "giant."
A custom Gespenst Mk-II, the classic mass-produced PT, from the PT upgrade plan "Project ATX." Model PTX-007-03C. Its fixed horizontal wings were replaced by
small variable-wing Tesla Drives and stabilizers, and its shoulder verniers by three-piece variable ones, greatly boosting mobility in space. Its own weapon is
the "Oxtongue Launcher," firing solid or beam rounds, making it a long-range unit. Focus on mobility made it very "fragile," and with high costs, only one prototype was made
and mass production died. Its code name from its color, "White Knight" (Weissritter), stuck.
The missing Weissritter, warped into an alien shape by otherworldly tech; over 60% of it defies analysis. It wields the Howling Launcher, likely a changed Oxtongue Launcher.
"Rein" is German for "pure."
A mystery enemy seemingly made of ogre masks, likely the only manned Einst. Ogre masks... What ties this unit of "masks," said to show "persona," to its pilot Alchemie...?
A mystery enemy that seems made of bone. With sharp claws and ribcage blades, it excels at close to mid range.
A mystery enemy that seems woven of plants or blood vessels. It fires a long-range beam from its face, but is weak up close.
A mystery enemy like Alteisen. Not just its looks, its weapons are nearly the same. What could that mean...?
A mystery enemy like Western armor. It looks sturdy, but it is utterly hollow inside. It seems high-ranking among them, and though its form is the most human,
being hollow inside is ironic.
Seemingly the Einst leader, with a giant body and power to match. Knochen, Glied, Gemut... It looks like the sum of all the Einst, but...?
Long ago, all life in the galaxy came from one planet: Earth. It is a system judging whether Earth's offspring will build a "peaceful universe." It aimed to "guide Earth's straying life
onto the right path," but slowly that aim went awry, and it moved to wipe out war-obsessed humanity and create a new universe.
Mass-production Gespenst, the classic PT behind Alteisen and Weissritter. Along with the Mega Beam Rifle, it has arms like the Mk-III-based Jet Magnum. But few were made,
and why it fights for the Einst is a total mystery. ...Indeed, it's unclear if this is really a "Gespenst Mk-II" at all...?
